tools.name: 3DCT
tools.approach: Affine 3D-to-2D coordinate transform with fiducial-based least-squares fit to map fluorescence z-stacks onto SEM/FIB images for site-specific cryo-FIB milling.
tools.when_to_use: Standard correlation tool for cryo-FIB site-specific milling guided by FLM z-stacks; widely used with SerialFIB and within METEOR workflows.
tools.limitations: Manual fiducial selection; accuracy limited by FLM PSF and fiducial visibility; classical only.
tools.verification_notes: Arnold, Mahamid, Lucic et al. Biophys. J. 110(4):860-869 (2016). py3DCT/v3 ports by Fung 2021.

tools.name: Appion
tools.approach: Database-driven web-managed processing pipeline that pairs with Leginon to provide automated on-the-fly micrograph QA, CTF, picking, and 2D/3D analysis.
tools.when_to_use: Facilities running Leginon that want a longstanding traceable processing log alongside acquisition; partially superseded by cryoSPARC Live for live work.
tools.limitations: Maintained but no longer the dominant on-the-fly stack; classical algorithms only.

tools.name: Arctis iFLM
tools.approach: Integrated widefield FLM module inside the Thermo Fisher Arctis Cryo-PFIB chamber; provides coincident fluorescence imaging at the FIB/SEM eucentric point for guided milling.
tools.when_to_use: Plasma FIB milling of large (e.g., tissue) cryo-samples with in-situ FLM guidance; current top-end commercial path.
tools.limitations: Commercial only; published characterization scattered across vendor materials and isolated demonstration papers.
tools.verification_notes: Berger, Walker et al. Nat. Commun. 14:629 (2023) describes plasma-FIB on a prototype Arctis. Citation for the iFLM specifically is mixed: Mam meeting abstracts (e.g., Microscopy and Microanalysis 2023) are the most explicit. Reviewer should choose the most accurate primary reference for chapter.

tools.name: ATUM
tools.approach: Modified ultramicrotome with a moving tape collector that captures thousands of consecutive ultrathin sections in order for downstream SEM/TEM imaging; foundation of large-volume connectomics.
tools.when_to_use: Volume EM workflows that prefer post-hoc multibeam SEM (MultiSEM) imaging of arrays rather than in-vacuo destruction by FIB/SBEM.
tools.limitations: Lossy section retrieval at very thin (<30 nm) sections; serial-section alignment harder than block-face EM.
tools.verification_notes: Hayworth, Morgan, Schalek et al. Front. Neural Circuits 8:68 (2014). AutoCUTS variant Kasthuri et al. Cell 2015. Verify the specific paper the chapter wants to cite (foundational vs application).

tools.name: AutoLamella
tools.approach: Python package for fully automated cryo-FIB lamella preparation built on the OpenFIBSEM API. Provides target selection, rough-to-fine milling protocols, and (since v2) plug-in points for ML-based feature detection of cells/organelles on the grid. Compatible with both ThermoFisher AutoScript and TESCAN Automation SDK.
tools.architecture: Workflow orchestrator + optional U-Net/SAM-style feature detectors as plug-in modules.
tools.training_paradigm: supervised (plug-in detectors); rule-based for milling logic
tools.training_data: Detector plug-ins use user-supplied annotated cryo-FIB grid views.
inputs: user-defined target list or detection map
tools.when_to_use: Open-source automated cryo-FIB milling at facility scale; preferred where vendor automation (AutoTEM/Stratos AutoLamella) is unavailable or where reproducible, scriptable, ML-extensible workflows are desired.
tools.limitations: Hardware support limited to ThermoFisher AutoScript and TESCAN Automation SDK; advanced ML targeting requires user-supplied models; not all microscopes are equally well tested.
tools.compute: Microscope control PC; GPU optional for ML targeting plug-ins.
tools.verification_notes: OpenFIBSEM publication (Cleeve P et al., J Struct Biol 215(3):107967, 2023, PMID 37105276) introduces AutoLamella v2 as the principal cryo-FIB workflow built on the API. The earlier 'AutoLamella' (Buckley et al., J Struct Biol 213(4):107799, 2020, PMID 33186717) is a separate Monash/Buckley package; the 2023 paper supersedes that line. No dedicated 2024 Nature Methods publication confirmed.

tools.name: BISECT
tools.approach: Beam image-shift accelerated tilt-series acquisition with per-tilt astigmatic CTF estimation and data-driven exposure weighting; precursor concept underpinning the BISECT data collection protocol for near-atomic in situ structures.
outputs: beam-image-shifted tilt series with per-tilt CTF and dose weighting
tools.when_to_use: Acquisition recipe for higher-throughput cryo-ET aiming at sub-nanometer-resolution structures; pre-dates PACE-tomo but offers the underlying logic (image-shift + geometry).
tools.limitations: Procedure-level paper rather than a standalone tool; requires SerialEM and the nextPYP/M downstream pipeline for full benefit.
tools.verification_notes: Bouvette, Liu, Huang et al. Nat. Commun. 12:1957 (2021). Recipe documented in Bartesaghi lab site.

tools.name: CASSPER
tools.approach: Semantic segmentation of micrographs into protein/ice/carbon/contamination classes; can be used at acquisition time for ice/carbon screening as well as for downstream particle picking.
tools.architecture: Full-Resolution Residual Network (FRRN) with residual + pooling streams.
tools.training_data: Visually-prepared training annotations on a small set of EMPIAR/in-house micrographs.
outputs: per-pixel class labels (protein, ice, carbon, etc.)
tools.when_to_use: Screening grids for ice vs carbon contamination; producing particle masks for downstream picking with reduced manual training.
tools.limitations: Small training set; class labels can be noisy; works well on holey-carbon imagery but degrades on novel grid types; community is small.
tools.verification_notes: George, Assaiya, Bhanot et al. Commun. Biol. 4:200 (2021). | DUP: canonical entry in stage 'segmentation'.

tools.name: CLEMSite
tools.subtask: CLEM target relocation and FIB-SEM automation
tools.approach: Software pipeline for automated phenotypic CLEM screens with FIB-SEM. CLEMSite-LM module identifies fluorescent targets on the grid, CLEMSite-EM Navigator + Multisite re-locates them in the SEM and triggers sequential FIB-SEM volume runs; a Run Checker module supervises long unattended jobs.
tools.architecture: Combines classical image registration with a CNN-based grid-square/landmark detection module.
tools.training_data: EMBL Carl-Zeiss-grid LM/SEM image pairs (in-house annotations).
tools.when_to_use: Room-temperature volume CLEM screens where many cells must be re-found in FIB-SEM without operator intervention; useful when adapting CLEM to medium-throughput discovery workflows.
tools.limitations: Optimised for Zeiss FIB-SEM (Crossbeam) and finder grids similar to those used at EMBL; cryo-CLEM workflows need adaptation; limited tested cells of biological diversity.
tools.compute: Microscope control workstation + 1 GPU for CNN inference.
tools.verification_notes: Serra Lleti JM, Steyer AM, Schieber NL et al., J Cell Biol 222(3):e202209127 (2023). PMID 36562752, DOI 10.1083/jcb.202209127. Russell/Schorb were not first authors as the gap entry suggested; first author is Serra Lleti, corresponding senior author Yannick Schwab.

tools.name: CorRelator
tools.approach: Interactive pixel-to-stage-coordinate transformation with live and post-acquisition correlation between cryo-FLM and TEM/ET; provides real-time positioning during data collection.
tools.when_to_use: Live correlative acquisition on non-integrated systems (standalone FLM + TEM) where 3DCT is insufficient for stage-driven retargeting.
tools.limitations: Designed for cryo-EM/ET only; not for FIB milling; 2D-centric correlation.
tools.verification_notes: Yang, Larson, Sibert, Shrum, Wright. JSB 213(2):107709 (2021).

tools.name: CryoFLARE
aliases: FMI Live Analysis and Reconstruction Engine
tools.approach: Modular open-source platform for live SPA pre-processing with pluggable algorithm modules and real-time visualization for monitoring microscope performance.

citation.venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

tools.when_to_use: Facilities that want a free, plug-and-play live monitor compatible with arbitrary motion/CTF/picker backends.
tools.limitations: Smaller community than cryoSPARC Live or Warp; no built-in ML.
tools.verification_notes: Schenk et al. (with Cavadini, Aebersold-affiliated and FMI group). J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2020. Verify exact author list before chapter — paper is sometimes cited as 'Schorb-adjacent EMBL pipeline' which is a different tool. | CORRECTION: Expert flagged this as 'wrong journal — should be Acta Cryst D'; verification (PubMed 32233514, Schenk et al. 2020) confirms the J Chem Inf Model citation is in fact correct. Schenk is the FMI Genoud-lab author. No CryoFLARE Acta Cryst D paper exists. Only the URL is updated to PubMed for resolvability and the verification note rewritten.

citation.venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

citation+verification_notes.verification_notes: Schenk AD, Cavadini S, Thomä NH, Genoud C. 'Live Analysis and Reconstruction of Single-Particle Cryo-Electron Microscopy Data with CryoFLARE.' J Chem Inf Model 60(5):2561-2569 (2020). PMID 32233514. The expert gap claim of an Acta Cryst D 2020 paper by Schenk et al. is incorrect — CryoFLARE was published in J Chem Inf Model and no Acta Cryst D paper exists. The current J Chem Inf Model citation is correct; PMID URL substituted for stability and authors verified.

tools.name: cryoSPARC Live
tools.approach: Streaming directory watcher that runs motion correction, CTF estimation, template/blob/deep particle picking, and initial 2D classification in real time during acquisition; CTF and visual quality used to reject exposures live.
tools.architecture: Bundled deep picker (Topaz-style) + classical motion/CTF.
tools.training_data: Bundled picker pretrained on internal Structura curated EMPIAR datasets.
tools.when_to_use: Real-time SPA monitoring during long Krios/Glacios sessions to catch drift, ice, contamination early; now bundled in Thermo Fisher Smart EPU.
tools.limitations: Closed-source freeware; throughput limited by GPU count (~450 exposures/h/GPU per docs); no separate Live paper - the 2017 Nat. Methods cryoSPARC paper is the canonical citation.
tools.license: Free academic; commercial license required for industry.
tools.verification_notes: No dedicated Live paper; cryoSPARC 2017 paper covers the platform. CryoSPARC Live documented in user guide and 2025 Microsc. Microanal. abstracts.

tools.name: DeepCLEM
tools.approach: CNN predicts in-silico fluorescent chromatin signal from EM micrographs; predicted images are correlated to experimental FLM signal to drive automatic CLEM registration.
tools.architecture: 2D U-Net trained for cross-modal image translation.
tools.training_data: Paired EM and FLM images of cell nuclei (HeLa, C. elegans, human skin) from the authors' lab.
tools.when_to_use: Automated 2D CLEM registration when chromatin stain is the fiducial; avoids manual fiducial picking.
tools.limitations: Trained mostly on nuclear/chromatin data; cross-domain generalization to other organelles or to cryo-CLEM unverified; 2D only.
tools.verification_notes: Seifert, Markert, Britz et al. F1000Research 9:1275 (2020), version 2 (2022).

tools.name: ENZEL
tools.approach: Custom retrofit of inverted widefield FLM + cryo-stage + positioning hardware onto an existing FIB-SEM to enable in-situ FLM-guided cryo-FIB milling without sample transfer.
tools.when_to_use: Custom-built integrated cryo-CLEM workflow; design reference for facilities exploring in-chamber FLM beyond commercial METEOR/iFLM systems.
tools.limitations: Custom build; reproduction non-trivial; cryo-FLM resolution limited by low-NA objective.
tools.verification_notes: Boltje, Hoogenboom, Jakobi et al. eLife 11:e82891 (2022) - 'A cryogenic, coincident fluorescence, electron, and ion beam microscope.' Sometimes referenced under the 'ENZEL' moniker; that name appears more frequently in earlier preprints. Reviewer should verify name match before citing.

tools.name: EPU / Smart EPU
tools.approach: Thermo Fisher's commercial SPA acquisition suite; recent 'Smart EPU' versions add AI-assisted hole/square selection, ice-thickness prediction, EPU Quality Monitor (EQM), and Embedded cryoSPARC Live.
tools.architecture: Proprietary classifiers; underlying architectures not disclosed in detail.
tools.training_data: Not publicly disclosed.
tools.when_to_use: Default SPA acquisition on Thermo Fisher Krios/Glacios/Talos Arctica scopes; Smart EPU is the vendor answer to Smart Leginon/SmartScope.
tools.limitations: No peer-reviewed publication describing model/training; vendor-only; closed weights; no independent benchmark.
tools.verification_notes: No peer-reviewed primary paper; documented only in Thermo Fisher data sheets and Microscopy & Microanalysis meeting abstracts (Grollios et al. 2024; Grollios et al. 2025 in Microsc. Microanal. 30/31 supplements). Be explicit in the chapter that Smart EPU is unpublished.

tools.name: Focus
tools.approach: High-throughput data-management and processing GUI bridging acquisition to RELION/MotionCor/CTFFIND/Frealign on direct detector output, with live status dashboards.
tools.when_to_use: On-the-fly pre-processing in facilities that prefer an open-source non-cryoSPARC stack; historically used at LBEM/EPFL and Basel.
tools.limitations: Development pace slowed post-2021; UI dated; mainly classical with no ML overlays.

tools.name: GridTape
tools.approach: Tape-based sample handling for automated serial-section TEM connectomics: laser-milled holes in aluminum-coated polyimide tape support thousands of ultrathin sections that can be auto-loaded onto a TEM stage.
tools.when_to_use: Large-volume connectomics requiring thousands of serial sections (Drosophila VNC, mouse cortex blocks); the Janelia/AIBS workflow.
tools.limitations: Requires custom stage + tape handling hardware; manufacture and adoption limited to a few labs.
tools.compute: TEM + control PC; downstream alignment requires HPC.
tools.verification_notes: Phelps, Hildebrand, Graham et al. Cell 184(3):759-774 (2021) is the canonical connectomics demonstration; underlying GridTape methods preprint Graham et al. bioRxiv 657346 (2019). A standalone methods paper for the TEM stage system itself has not appeared - chapter should cite both.

tools.name: Hagen dose-symmetric tilt scheme
tools.approach: Tilt-series ordering that begins near zero tilt and alternates outward to positive and negative angles; preserves high-frequency information at low-dose early frames for sub-tomogram averaging.
tools.when_to_use: Default tilt-scheme for high-resolution sub-tomogram averaging; benchmark studies (Turonova et al. 2020) confirm advantage over bidirectional/unidirectional schemes.
tools.limitations: Slightly slower per tilt-series than bidirectional schemes; gains realized only for STA workflows that exploit high-frequency early frames.
tools.verification_notes: Hagen, Wan, Briggs. JSB 197(2):191-198 (2017). Widely adopted and cited.

tools.name: JADAS
tools.approach: JEOL's automated SPA acquisition platform built on the TemServer protocol; coordinates microscope, camera, and piezo-stage for ice-embedded particle imaging under low dose.
tools.when_to_use: JEOL CRYO ARM and JEM-3200FSC platforms when SerialEM JEOL plugin is not used.
tools.limitations: Vendor lock-in to JEOL; no ML overlays; community is smaller than SerialEM's.
tools.verification_notes: Zhang, Nakamura, Shimizu et al. JSB 165(1):1-9 (2009).

tools.name: Latitude S
tools.approach: Gatan's automated SPA acquisition software, tightly integrated with K3/K2 cameras and BioContinuum/BioQuantum filters; supports image-shift collection and on-the-fly addition of grid areas.
inputs: TEM state via Gatan camera control
tools.when_to_use: Facilities running Gatan detector ecosystems that prefer vendor automation; works with Thermo Fisher, JEOL, Hitachi TEMs.
tools.limitations: No peer-reviewed primary citation; closed-source; less feature-rich than SerialEM scripting.
tools.verification_notes: Vendor-only documentation. Cite as 'Gatan, Inc.' product.

tools.name: Leginon
tools.approach: Modular, distributed-process architecture for automated TEM acquisition with a relational database back-end; supports multi-scale targeting and image-shift collection.
tools.when_to_use: SPA acquisition in shared facilities needing per-session traceability and multi-user database support; canonical pairing with Appion downstream pipeline.
tools.limitations: Steeper installation than SerialEM; classical hole/square selection; ML overlays require Smart Leginon/Ptolemy.
tools.compute: Acquisition workstation plus DB server; no GPU.
tools.verification_notes: Primary Suloway et al. 2005 JSB verified. Cheng et al. (2021) 'Leginon: new features and applications' Protein Sci. 30:136-150 documents recent updates.

tools.name: METEOR
tools.approach: Integrated fluorescence light microscope retrofit inside a cryo-FIB/SEM chamber that allows in-situ FLM imaging at the eucentric height between milling steps; commercial instrument with peer-reviewed validation.
inputs: fluorescent reporter expressed in vitrified cells
tools.when_to_use: Routine fluorescence-guided lamella milling without sample transfer; reduces contamination versus shuttle workflows.
tools.limitations: Commercial only; limited objective NA versus dedicated cryo-FLM (e.g., Aquilos iFLM); fluorescence acquisition slower than top-down systems.
tools.verification_notes: Smeets et al. Microscopy Today / Microsc. Microanal. 28(S1) coverage. The most-cited paper is the Microscopy Today piece; check for a more recent peer-reviewed methods paper (e.g., Boltje et al. or Last et al. via Delmic) before chapter inclusion.

tools.name: MicAssess
tools.approach: ResNet-34 classifier predicts 'good'/'bad' micrographs from full-frame images; hierarchical sub-classification adds quality categories.
tools.architecture: ResNet-34 CNN.
tools.training_data: Curated labeled micrographs from the Cianfrocco lab (COSMIC2 service), several hundred labeled examples per class.
tools.when_to_use: Live or post-hoc rejection of unusable micrographs to improve downstream 2D/3D throughput; classical alternative to CTF-based filtering.
tools.limitations: Trained on holey-carbon SPA datasets; degraded performance on cryo-ET or unusual specimens; reported ~93% accuracy on validation set but inter-annotator variability not quantified. Recent Miffi (Xu & Ando 2024) reports improved accuracy.
tools.compute: Single GPU sufficient; CPU-only inference possible.
tools.verification_notes: Li, Cash, Flanagan, Cianfrocco. Structure 28(7):858-869 (2020). Sometimes referenced as 'MicAssess 1.0' (Li & Cianfrocco 2021); verify which version of the model is cited. | DUP: canonical entry in stage 'processing'.

tools.name: Miffi
tools.approach: CNN classifier that ingests both real-space micrograph and its power spectrum to predict four label categories (support film coverage, drift, crystallinity, contamination); fine-tuning improves over MicAssess.
tools.architecture: Pre-trained ImageNet CNN backbone fine-tuned with dual-channel (real + Fourier) input.
tools.training_data: EMPIAR datasets labeled across four categories; details in paper supplement.
tools.when_to_use: Improved live/post-hoc micrograph filtering when MicAssess-style binary classification is insufficient; integrates with Scipion via scipion-em-miffi plugin.
tools.limitations: Like MicAssess, trained primarily on SPA holey-carbon imagery; generalization to cryo-ET or unusual grids not characterized; small risk of dropping rare but valid images.
tools.verification_notes: Xu & Ando. JSB 216(2):108072 (2024). | DUP: canonical entry in stage 'processing'.

tools.name: MultiSEM
tools.approach: Parallel acquisition with 61 (or more) electron beams in a single column with parallel secondary-electron detectors; near two orders of magnitude throughput gain over single-beam SEM.
tools.when_to_use: Petabyte-scale connectomics acquisitions (H01 human cortex, MICrONS, FlyEM); only practical option for cubic-millimeter mouse-cortex datasets.
tools.limitations: Capital-intensive ($M+) instrument; available at only a handful of sites; per-beam alignment and stitching are non-trivial.
tools.verification_notes: Eberle, Mikula, Schalek et al. J. Microsc. 259(2):114-120 (2015). H01 (Shapson-Coe 2024) and MICrONS papers cite this instrument.

tools.name: PACE-tomo
tools.approach: SerialEM Python scripts that fit a geometrical sample model to multiple targets and use beam image-shift to collect tens of tilt series in parallel per stage position, reaching <5 min/tilt-series throughput.
tools.when_to_use: High-throughput cryo-ET on lamellae or thin specimens to multiply effective targets per stage move; default tilt-scheme: dose-symmetric.
tools.limitations: Requires careful calibration of image-shift coma compensation; geometrical model assumes a planar lamella; quality drops at large image-shift distances.
tools.verification_notes: Eisenstein, Yanagisawa, Kashihara, Kikkawa, Tsukita, Danev. Nat. Methods 20:131-138 (2023). EMPIAR-11111 deposited.

tools.name: PIE-scope
tools.approach: Custom-built integrated cryo-FIB+SEM+light microscope in a single chamber; enables real-time fluorescence checking during lamella milling without sample transfer.
tools.when_to_use: Reference academic implementation of in-chamber cryo-FLM for FIB; design papers basis for current commercial systems.
tools.limitations: Custom prototype; only a few sites have built equivalents; method paper rather than packaged software.
tools.verification_notes: Gorelick, Buckley, Gervinskas et al. eLife 8:e45919 (2019). Follow-up protocol paper (Gorelick et al. 2021) in Methods Mol. Biol.

tools.name: Ptolemy
tools.approach: Multi-scale targeting pipeline: Gaussian mixture models for grid-square segmentation, CNN/U-Net for hole detection, and a ranker that ordering squares and holes by predicted yield without session-specific tuning.
tools.architecture: CNN + U-Net (segmentation) + mixture-model components.
tools.training_data: SEMC/NYSBC sessions (held-out grids) plus external NIEHS held-out set; mix of holey-carbon and gold foils.
outputs: ranked square and hole targets with confidence scores
tools.when_to_use: Drop-in target selector for Leginon (via Smart Leginon) or standalone evaluation of grid-square/hole quality; useful when an external scoring service for hole quality is needed.
tools.limitations: Class set limited to common holey-carbon and Au foils; trained against expert-labeled targets that themselves carry annotator variability; confidence scores not formally calibrated.
tools.compute: Single GPU recommended; CPU inference possible at the cost of speed.
tools.verification_notes: Kim et al. IUCrJ 10(1):90-102 (2023). arXiv preprint 2112.01534 (2021) is the earlier version.

tools.name: SerialEM
tools.approach: Robust prediction of specimen movement for automated tilt-series and SPA acquisition; scriptable Python/macro interface; vendor-agnostic (Tecnai/Titan, JEOL, Hitachi).
tools.when_to_use: Default open-source automation for SPA and cryo-ET on most TEM platforms; foundation for many downstream scripts (PACE-tomo, SPACEtomo, Smart Leginon scripts).
tools.limitations: Classical, no built-in ML; scripting still required for many workflows; UI dated.
tools.compute: Modest control PC; no GPU required for acquisition.
tools.verification_notes: Canonical primary paper Mastronarde 2005 JSB verified. Earlier short Microsc. Microanal. 9(S2):1182-1183 (2003) was a meeting paper. Active development at Boulder Lab.

tools.name: SerialFIB
tools.approach: Open-source automation suite for cryo-FIB instruments: GUI plus Python scripting module that performs automated lamella milling, FIB-SEM volume tomography, and 3D-CLEM-guided protocols by interfacing with 3DCT.
tools.when_to_use: Automated lamella preparation on Thermo Fisher Aquilos/Arctis when vendor AutoTEM/AutoSlicer is unavailable or insufficient; supports CLEM-guided milling.
tools.limitations: Tightly coupled to specific FIB-SEM xT control APIs; user must build calibration; no ML site selection (separate AI is needed).
tools.verification_notes: Klumpe, Fung, Goetz et al. eLife 10:e70506 (2021). Mahamid lab + Plitzko lab collaboration. | CORRECTION: Expert flagged type label; verification additionally surfaced that the venue listed in the entry was Nature Communications, which is incorrect — the actual publication is in eLife (Klumpe et al., eLife 10:e70506, 2021). Both fields require correction.

type + verification_notes.verification_notes: Klumpe S, Fung HKH, Goetz SK et al. 'A modular platform for automated cryo-FIB workflows.' eLife 10:e70506 (2021). PMID 34951584. Note: the original entry incorrectly listed Nature Communications as the venue — the canonical SerialFIB paper is in eLife 2021. Type updated from 'classical' to 'hybrid' because newer SerialFIB releases integrate ML target detection via SPACEtomo/AutoLamella plug-in points.

tools.name: Smart Leginon
tools.approach: ML-enabled multi-grid screening overlay on Leginon that calls Ptolemy for square/hole detection and uses image-template matching to reproduce expert decisions across grids without manual setup per grid.
tools.architecture: Wraps Ptolemy (mixture models + CNN/U-Net) for square and hole detection.
tools.training_data: SEMC/NYSBC archive (holey carbon and UltrAuFoil grids); also tested on external NIEHS dataset.
tools.when_to_use: Overnight unattended multi-grid screening on Krios/Glacios within an NYSBC-style Leginon setup; reduces operator time from ~6 h to <10 min per session as reported in the paper.
tools.limitations: Best for grid types resembling training data (holey carbon, UltrAuFoil); calibration drift across instruments; vendor lock-in to Leginon ecosystem.
tools.compute: Inherits Leginon control PC requirements + Ptolemy inference (single GPU optional).
tools.verification_notes: Cheng et al. IUCrJ 10(1):77-89 (2023) verified. Bioxiv preprint v2 dated 2023-07.

tools.name: SmartScope
tools.approach: Deep-learning-based object detection at multiple magnifications classifies squares, holes, and ice-thickness suitability; web interface enables remote review and human-in-the-loop retraining of feature classifiers.
tools.architecture: Object-detection CNN (Faster-R-CNN-style) for squares/holes; classification heads for thickness.
tools.training_data: Curated NIEHS/Duke sessions across multiple grid types; annotated by acquisition experts.
outputs: automated low-dose collection on suitable grids
tools.when_to_use: Automated multi-grid screening and collection on Thermo Fisher Krios/Glacios driven by SerialEM; first published end-to-end screening framework with retrainable feature recognition.
tools.limitations: Networks evaluated on Duke/NIEHS-style sessions; may need retraining on novel grid coatings or specimens; integration deepest with SerialEM rather than Leginon/EPU.
tools.compute: GPU recommended for retraining; inference modest.
tools.verification_notes: Bouvette et al. eLife 11:e80047 (2022). Active GitHub commits 2024-2025.

tools.name: SPACEtomo
tools.approach: Adds deep-learning lamella detection, biological-feature segmentation, and automated target selection on top of PACE-tomo to drive fully unattended cryo-ET from grid square to tilt-series.
tools.architecture: U-Net-style segmentation for lamellae and intra-lamella organelle features (model details in supplement).
tools.training_data: Curated EMBL/U. Tokyo lamellae imagery (in-paper).
outputs: selected targets and parallel PACE-tomo collection
tools.when_to_use: Unattended cryo-ET sessions on FIB-milled lamellae where biological feature targeting (mitochondria, vesicles, etc.) is desired; key advance in cryo-ET acquisition automation 2024.
tools.limitations: Models trained predominantly on yeast/mammalian lamellae; generalization to bacterial or plant cells unverified; depends on lamella image quality.
tools.compute: Single modern GPU (Volta or newer) for inference on the acquisition PC.
tools.verification_notes: Eisenstein, Fukuda, Danev. Nat. Methods 21:1612-1615 (2024).

tools.name: Tomo Live
tools.approach: On-the-fly tilt-series alignment and reconstruction during acquisition; provides immediate tomogram quality assessment to the operator.
tools.when_to_use: Live triage during cryo-ET sessions on Thermo Fisher scopes running Tomo5; reduces wasted screen time on poor lamellae.
tools.limitations: Commercial only; reported algorithms are classical IMOD/AreTomo-style.
tools.verification_notes: Comet et al. Acta Cryst. D80(4):247-258 (2024). Verify the exact author list (multiple Thermo Fisher authors).

tools.name: Tomo5
tools.approach: Thermo Fisher's commercial cryo-ET acquisition software; supports multigrid sessions, beam image-shift acquisition (PACE-tomo-like geometry), and integrates with Tomo Live for reconstruction.
tools.when_to_use: Default Thermo Fisher cryo-ET acquisition where vendor support and Tomo Live are required.
tools.limitations: No peer-reviewed paper; closed-source; less flexible than SerialEM+PACE-tomo for advanced research workflows.
tools.compute: Acquisition PC + Tomo Live GPU server.
tools.verification_notes: Documented only in vendor data sheets and Microsc. Microanal. abstracts (Grollios et al. 2025).

tools.name: TOMOMAN
tools.approach: MATLAB-based wrapper that imports raw tilt-series, manages per-series metadata in HDF, and routes data through external motion correction, CTF estimation, alignment (IMOD, AreTomo), and reconstruction packages. Pipeline-agnostic, designed for inter-package data transfer between Warp/RELION3, RELION 4/5 tomo and STOPGAP.
tools.when_to_use: Cryo-ET facility-scale preprocessing managing many concurrent tilt-series and moving them between heterogeneous downstream tools (Warp/M, RELION, STOPGAP). Strongly recommended downstream of PACE-tomo data sets.
tools.limitations: MATLAB dependency limits free-software stacks; primarily authored for Wan/Beck-lab workflows.
tools.compute: Workstation with MATLAB Runtime; GPU only if delegating to GPU-backed wrappers.
tools.verification_notes: Khavnekar S, Erdmann PS, Wan W. 'TOMOMAN: a software package for large-scale cryo-electron tomography data preprocessing, community data sharing and collaborative computing.' IUCrJ 11(Pt 6):978-988 (2024). PMC11092592. Authorship is Wan lab (Vanderbilt) plus MPI-Biochemistry, not the Wagner lab as listed in the gap text.

tools.name: TranSPHIRE
tools.approach: Automated on-the-fly SPA pipeline that wraps MotionCor2, CTFFIND, crYOLO, and SPHIRE 2D/3D jobs with a feedback loop that re-trains crYOLO on the live dataset.
tools.architecture: crYOLO (YOLO-family detector) re-trained live.
tools.training_data: Bundled crYOLO general model + session-specific retraining on user-labeled positives.
tools.when_to_use: Single-workstation on-the-fly pipeline for SPA when SPHIRE/crYOLO are preferred; useful when no GPU farm is available.
tools.limitations: MPI-Dortmund-centric stack; classification feedback loop hard to integrate with other suites; less actively maintained than cryoSPARC Live/Warp.
tools.verification_notes: Stabrin, Schoenfeld, Wagner et al. Nat. Commun. 11:5716 (2020). Repo: MPI-Dortmund.

tools.name: Warp
tools.approach: Real-time motion correction, local CTF estimation, deep-learning denoising, and CNN-based particle picking ('BoxNet'); monitors acquisition session and produces RELION/cryoSPARC-ready particle stacks.
tools.architecture: BoxNet (2D U-Net) for picking; classical patch-based motion + CTF.
tools.training_data: BoxNet trained on a curated set of ~50 EMPIAR datasets with synthetic augmentation.
tools.when_to_use: Live preprocessing during SPA/cryo-ET acquisition; pairs with M for tilt-series-level refinement downstream.
tools.limitations: Windows-only historically (now Linux ports in WarpEM/WarpCore); BoxNet bias toward training-set particle classes.
tools.compute: 1 GPU per Warp instance; recommended >=11 GB VRAM.
tools.verification_notes: Tegunov & Cramer Nat. Methods 16:1146-1152 (2019). Successor (Warp 2/WarpEM with Linux/M2) documented 2023-2024. | DUP: canonical entry in stage 'processing'.

tools.name: alignframes (IMOD)
tools.approach: Whole-frame and optional patch-tracking alignment of movie frames within the IMOD package, with options for dark/gain correction and binning; pairs with Etomo for tilt-series workflows.

citation.venue: Journal of Structural Biology (companion to the etomo auto-alignment paper)

inputs: MRC movie or tilt-series frame stack
tools.when_to_use: When the rest of the pipeline lives in IMOD/Etomo (especially classical fiducial-based tomography); enables a single-suite workflow.
tools.limitations: Less GPU acceleration than MotionCor2/3; documented best for tilt-series frame alignment rather than high-end SPA movies.
tools.last_meaningful_update: IMOD 4.12 (2024-2025) continues maintenance at Boulder Lab.
tools.verification_notes: Mastronarde & Held (2017) JSB 197:102-113 is the canonical 'Automated tilt series alignment and tomographic reconstruction in IMOD' paper that documents the modern alignframes tooling chain (PMID 27444392).

tools.name: AlignParts_LMBFGS
tools.approach: Per-particle movie alignment posed as an optimization: maximizes correlation between Fourier transforms of individual frames and the all-frame sum, solved with the L-BFGS quasi-Newton algorithm; per-particle trajectories smoothed locally to enforce spatial continuity.
tools.when_to_use: Historic per-particle motion correction; conceptually superseded by RELION's Bayesian polishing and cryoSPARC's local motion correction but still cited as the methodological ancestor.
tools.limitations: No GPU support; per-particle local trajectories assume mild deviation from whole-frame motion; rarely used in 2026 outside legacy pipelines.
tools.verification_notes: Rubinstein JL & Brubaker MA (2015) JSB 192:188-195 verified via the arXiv preprint 1409.6789 and Sciencedirect; PMID 26296328.

tools.name: AlignTK
tools.approach: Toolkit (C/Perl) for serial-section EM montage and alignment combining feature-based affine alignment with iterative elastic warping; long-time mainstay of Bock-lab and other connectomics groups before SOFIMA.
tools.when_to_use: Where existing lab pipelines depend on AlignTK; otherwise SOFIMA is preferred for new volumes.
tools.limitations: No definitive peer-reviewed method paper; usage documented mainly through Bock et al. 2011 and downstream Janelia/Pitt project papers. Limited active development.
tools.license: Open source (custom license; redistributed by MMBIOS).
tools.verification_notes: AlignTK does not have a clean canonical journal paper. Researchers typically cite Bock DD et al. 2011 Nature 471:177-182 (which describes its use) or the MMBIOS documentation. Flag for the writer: do not present as a single-paper tool.

tools.name: AreTomo
tools.approach: GPU-accelerated fiducial-less (and fiducial-aware) tilt-series alignment via iterative projection matching against a coarsely reconstructed tomogram volume. Performs local motion correction, alignment, sample-tilt and rotation estimation, and back-projection or SIRT reconstruction in one binary.
tools.when_to_use: Default fiducial-less alignment for cellular cryo-ET and lamellae where IMOD's marker-based workflow is impractical; the workhorse step between Warp/RELION preprocessing and STA.
tools.limitations: Projection matching can fail on extremely low-SNR or thick samples; no CTF or live-pipeline features (use AreTomo3/Live instead).
tools.compute: Single GPU (~12 GB VRAM minimum); multi-GPU supported in v2.
tools.verification_notes: Zheng S, Wolff G, Greenan G, Chen Z, Faas FGA, Bárcena M, Koster AJ, Cheng Y, Agard DA. J Struct Biol X 6:100068 (2022). PMID 35601683, DOI 10.1016/j.yjsbx.2022.100068. This is the canonical AreTomo paper; AreTomo3 and AreTomoLive (below) are separate, more recent code lines. | DUP: canonical entry in stage 'data_analysis'.

tools.name: AreTomo3
tools.approach: Integrated multi-GPU pipeline merging the functions of MotionCor3, AreTomo2 and GCtfFind into one autonomous application: global+local beam-induced motion correction, defocus-handedness determination, sample-geometry estimation, local CTF correction, alignment, and reconstruction, run in parallel with data collection.
tools.when_to_use: On-the-fly cryo-ET pipelines at the microscope; recommended for high-throughput tomography and as a feed to RELION-5 / Warp 2 / nextPYP.
tools.limitations: No peer-reviewed publication separate from the AreTomoLive preprint as of 2026-05; benchmarking still community-driven; GPU-heavy.
tools.verification_notes: AreTomo3 is described jointly with DenoisET in the AreTomoLive preprint (Peck A, Yu Y, Paraan M, Kimanius D, et al., bioRxiv 2025.03.11.642690, 2025-03). No standalone Stabrin-Zheng 2024 IUCrJ paper was located; expert gap suggestion appears incorrect on that citation.

tools.name: AreTomoLive
tools.approach: Pipeline bundling AreTomo3 with the DenoisET Noise2Noise-style denoiser to deliver fully reconstructed and contrast-enhanced tomograms within minutes of acquisition. Includes a curation interface for live QA and downstream export to RELION/Warp.
tools.architecture: Classical AreTomo3 alignment + denoising CNN (Noise2Noise-style).
tools.training_paradigm: self_supervised (DenoisET module trained on even/odd splits)
tools.training_data: Per-dataset self-supervision; no static training corpus required.
tools.when_to_use: Microscope-side live tomography: judging tilt-series quality, on-the-fly selection for STA, sessions where decisions must be made within minutes.
tools.limitations: Preprint only; pipeline reliability depends on GPU bandwidth and AreTomo3 stability; limited testing on non-CZII data ecosystems.
tools.verification_notes: AreTomoLive preprint: Peck, Yu, Paraan, Kimanius et al., bioRxiv 2025.03.11.642690 (2025-03). No peer-reviewed version yet.

tools.name: Bayesian polishing (RELION)
tools.approach: Per-particle beam-induced motion modeled as a Gaussian process with priors that enforce spatial and temporal smoothness; jointly fits B-factor radiation-damage weights as a function of dose and resolution. Replaces older RELION particle polishing.
tools.when_to_use: Final post-MotionCor refinement step before high-resolution 3D refinement in RELION; essential for sub-3 A SPA reconstructions in most pipelines.
tools.limitations: Requires upstream pose estimates; sensitive to bad particle classes; runtime non-trivial for large datasets.
tools.last_meaningful_update: RELION 5 (2024) extends Bayesian polishing concepts to tilt-series-level refinement.
tools.verification_notes: Zivanov J, Nakane T, Scheres SHW. IUCrJ 6:5-17 (2019) verified PMID 30713699.

tools.name: cryo-CARE
tools.approach: Noise2Noise-style content-aware denoising: trains a U-Net to map one noisy realization (even-frame sum or even-frame tomogram) to a paired independent noisy realization (odd-frame sum/tomogram), exploiting independence of shot noise between halves.
tools.architecture: 2D and 3D U-Net (encoder-decoder CNN with skip connections; CARE/CSBDeep lineage).
tools.training_data: Even/odd movie-frame splits of the user's own dataset; no external labels.
inputs: paired even/odd movie sums (2D) or even/odd tomograms (3D)
tools.when_to_use: Cryo-ET tomogram visualization and downstream segmentation; SPA micrograph denoising for visualization (not for downstream refinement, which would risk FSC inflation).
tools.limitations: Requires paired even/odd realizations; risks artificially correlating half-maps if used inside the SPA refinement loop; visual improvement does not guarantee resolution gain.
tools.compute: Single GPU; 8-24 GB VRAM depending on patch size.
tools.verification_notes: Buchholz T-O, Jordan M, Pigino G, Jug F. Proc. IEEE ISBI 2019:502-506 verified DOI 10.1109/ISBI.2019.8759519; arXiv 1810.05420.

tools.name: CryoFM
tools.subtask: foundation model / generative prior for density maps
tools.approach: Flow-matching generative foundation model trained on EMDB density maps that learns a prior over cryo-EM densities. Downstream tasks (denoising, missing-wedge filling, map sharpening, ab initio guidance) are recast as flow-posterior-sampling problems against this prior, requiring no per-task retraining.
tools.architecture: U-Net-style score/velocity backbone with 3D inputs; trained with flow matching.
tools.training_data: Curated subset of EMDB density maps.
outputs: sampled posterior density volumes for the downstream task
tools.when_to_use: Plug-and-play prior for low-SNR/incomplete cryo-EM maps; alternative to bespoke task-specific networks; principled for missing-wedge filling and density modification.
tools.limitations: Computationally heavy at inference (iterative sampling); validation primarily on synthetic and benchmark data; behaviour on cellular cryo-ET still being established.
tools.compute: GPU (>=24 GB VRAM); inference is iterative.
tools.verification_notes: Yu C, Wang Z, Wei J et al. 'CryoFM: A Flow-based Foundation Model for Cryo-EM Densities.' ICLR 2025; arXiv:2410.08631. Westlake AI / Westlake University authorship.

tools.name: CryoGEM
tools.approach: Physics-informed generative model that simulates cryo-EM imaging from a virtual specimen and then uses contrastive-learning-based unpaired noise translation (mask-guided sampling) to inject realistic noise distributions. Outputs are physically-correct synthetic micrographs suitable as training data for pickers, pose estimators, and denoisers.
tools.architecture: Physics simulator + contrastive unpaired image-to-image translation (CUT/CycleGAN family); not a diffusion model.
tools.training_data: Real cryo-EM micrographs used only for unpaired style learning; ground-truth particle locations come from the simulator.

citation.venue: NeurIPS (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems)

outputs: synthetic cryo-EM micrographs with ground-truth particle metadata
tools.when_to_use: Augmenting picker/pose-estimator training when annotated micrographs are scarce; pretraining foundation models for cryo-EM where real labelled data is limited.
tools.limitations: Not a diffusion model despite generative framing; style transfer can fail on imaging conditions outside the training distribution; downstream improvement is task-specific.
tools.compute: GPU (>=16 GB VRAM) for training; inference fast.
tools.verification_notes: Zhang J et al. 'CryoGEM: Physics-Informed Generative Cryo-Electron Microscopy.' NeurIPS 2024. arXiv:2312.02235. Not in Nature Methods as suggested in gap text.

tools.name: cryoSPARC Live
tools.approach: Live on-the-fly preprocessing (motion correction, CTF, picking, 2D class) inside cryoSPARC, with continuous micrograph QA and exposure curation as data stream in.

citation.venue: Nature Methods (cryoSPARC); Live feature documented in cryoSPARC guide and unpublished talks

outputs: live processing dashboard, live QA flags, exposure curation
tools.when_to_use: Live SPA session monitoring at facilities running cryoSPARC; preferred over Warp Live for cryoSPARC-centric pipelines.
tools.limitations: Closed source; subset of cryoSPARC algorithms; commercial license required for non-academic users.
tools.verification_notes: No peer-reviewed Live-specific paper; cite the 2017 algorithms paper for the underlying methods and the cryoSPARC guide for Live behavior. | DUP: canonical entry in stage 'acquisition'.

tools.name: cryoSPARC patch motion correction
tools.approach: cryoSPARC's in-suite GPU motion correction, similar in spirit to MotionCor2 (patch-based local motion); paired with Patch CTF estimation. Documented in the cryoSPARC user guide rather than in the algorithms paper, which focuses on reconstruction.

citation.venue: Nature Methods (the foundational cryoSPARC algorithms paper)

tools.when_to_use: Within a cryoSPARC-only pipeline where running external tools is undesirable; closely matched performance to MotionCor2.
tools.limitations: Closed-source freeware (Structura Biotechnology); algorithmic details only partially published; commercial license required for paid users.
tools.license: cryoSPARC EULA (free academic; commercial license required for paid users)
integration_targets: import from Patch CTF to RELION
tools.verification_notes: The algorithms paper (Punjani et al. 2017) covers ab-initio and refinement; patch motion correction is documented in the cryoSPARC user guide. Cite the 2017 paper plus the guide URL when needed.

tools.name: CTFFIND4
tools.approach: Fits a parametric CTF model to the rotational average and 2D power spectrum of a micrograph; uses fast 1D search followed by 2D refinement to estimate defocus, astigmatism, and (with phase plates) phase shift.
tools.when_to_use: Default open-source CTF estimator for SPA and tilt-series; reliable, fast, well-validated; the workhorse for >99% of cryo-EM facilities.
tools.limitations: Assumes thin, untilted sample; degrades on highly tilted or thick specimens (addressed by CTFFIND5).
tools.last_meaningful_update: Maintained inside cisTEM; CTFFIND5 supersedes for tilted/thick samples.
tools.verification_notes: Rohou A & Grigorieff N (2015) JSB 192:216-221 verified PMID 26278980.

tools.name: CTFFIND5
tools.approach: Extends CTFFIND4 with (a) patch-wise CTF fits to estimate sample tilt directly from a single micrograph (claimed 3-degree accuracy), and (b) a modified CTF model accounting for sample thickness (claimed 5 nm accuracy). Validated on tilted 2D aquaporin crystals and FIB-milled cell lamellae.
inputs: micrograph MRC, optionally a per-tilt stack
outputs: defocus, astigmatism, phase shift, estimated sample tilt and thickness
tools.when_to_use: Cryo-FIB lamella micrographs, tilted SPA collections, thick in-situ samples; whenever CTFFIND4 underperforms because of tilt or thickness.
tools.limitations: Slower than CTFFIND4 at default settings; tilt and thickness estimates depend on power-spectrum quality.
tools.last_meaningful_update: Final eLife publication December 2024; bioRxiv version Feb 2024.
tools.verification_notes: Elferich J, Kong S, Zhang Q, Sigworth FJ, Grigorieff N. eLife 13:e97227 (2024) verified PMID 39704651 / DOI 10.7554/eLife.97227.

tools.name: DeepDeWedge
tools.approach: Self-supervised joint denoising and missing-wedge filling. A randomly-initialized 3D U-Net is fit per tomogram with a self-supervised loss that uses both even/odd subsets of tilts and synthetic wedge masking; combines Noise2Noise and missing-wedge-masking objectives.
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net.
tools.training_data: Two reconstructions from disjoint tilt subsets of the same tomogram (no external labels).
inputs: paired-subset tilt reconstructions of a single tomogram
tools.when_to_use: Cryo-ET tomograms with extreme missing-wedge artifacts where IsoNet under-performs; particularly for thick in-situ samples.
tools.limitations: Per-tomogram fit (no pretrained weights); hallucination warning identical to IsoNet; runtime can be hours.
tools.compute: GPU with 24+ GB VRAM for typical tomograms.
tools.last_meaningful_update: Final Nat Commun publication 2024; v3 arXiv 2311.05539 updated 2024.
tools.verification_notes: Wiedemann S & Heckel R. Nat Commun 15:8255 (2024) verified DOI 10.1038/s41467-024-51438-y; arXiv 2311.05539. | DUP: canonical entry in stage 'data_analysis'.

tools.name: DenoisET
tools.approach: Noise2Noise implementation tailored to cryo-ET tomograms; designed for live-acquisition integration with AreTomo3/AreTomoLive: it auto-selects training tomograms and transitions from training to inference during streaming acquisition.
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net (Noise2Noise objective).
tools.training_data: Even/odd tomogram reconstructions emitted by AreTomo3 during acquisition.
inputs: paired even/odd tomograms from AreTomo3 / AreTomoLive
tools.when_to_use: Live cryo-ET acquisition at facilities running AreTomoLive; alternative to cryoCARE-tomo with simpler integration.
tools.limitations: Preprint-stage at time of writing; tied to AreTomo3 outputs; no large-scale validation outside the AreTomoLive paper.
tools.verification_notes: DenoisET appears to lack a dedicated standalone paper; described in the AreTomoLive preprint (Peck A et al., 2025). Verify the AreTomoLive citation before chapter inclusion.

tools.name: EER (Electron-Event Representation)
tools.approach: Per-electron event encoding (x,y,frame-time) at sub-pixel and high temporal resolution; supports flexible re-fractionation at processing time. Strictly a file format and frame-handling convention rather than an algorithm, but it shapes how all downstream motion-correction and dose-weighting tools operate.
tools.when_to_use: Acquisition output of all Falcon 4/4i sessions in 2024-2026; processed by MotionCor3, Warp, RELION 5, and cryoSPARC with native EER ingestion.
tools.limitations: Requires updated readers; vendor-specific format though documented publicly.
tools.license: Format publicly documented (Thermo Fisher / SickKids); open readers in MotionCor3 and others.
tools.verification_notes: Guo H, Franken E, Deng Y, Benlekbir S, Singla Lezcano G, Janssen B et al. IUCrJ 7:860-869 (2020) verified PMID 32939278.

tools.name: Fiji Linear Stack Alignment with SIFT
tools.approach: Scale-Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT) keypoint extraction and matching across consecutive sections, followed by a least-squares affine or rigid transform per section. Distributed as a Fiji plugin.

citation.venue: International Journal of Computer Vision (foundational SIFT paper)

tools.when_to_use: First-pass rough alignment of small vEM stacks; pedagogical default in Fiji; rarely sufficient as final alignment for connectomics.
tools.limitations: No non-linear warping; fails on highly deformed sections; reference SIFT paper is computer-vision rather than EM-specific.
tools.last_meaningful_update: Maintained as Fiji plugin; methodology stable.
tools.verification_notes: Canonical SIFT reference is Lowe DG (2004) IJCV 60:91-110. The Fiji plugin is documented at imagej.net and uses Saalfeld's implementation.

tools.name: Gctf
tools.approach: GPU-accelerated CTF estimation by maximizing cross-correlation between simulated CTF and log-amplitude spectrum after background subtraction; introduces equiphase averaging (EPA) and a 1D-search+2D-refinement strategy. Supports per-particle and per-frame local refinement.
tools.when_to_use: Faster than CTFFIND4 on GPUs (10-50x); historically common for per-particle defocus refinement.
tools.limitations: Closed-source binary distributed by author; minimally maintained since ~2018; per-particle refinement now offered natively by cryoSPARC/RELION.
tools.last_meaningful_update: Final public binary 1.18 (2018); no active development.
tools.verification_notes: Zhang K (2016) JSB 193:1-12 verified PMID 26592709.

tools.name: IsoNet
tools.approach: Iterative deep learning for joint missing-wedge restoration and denoising of single cryo-ET tomograms. Trains a 3D U-Net to predict full-tomogram structure from versions in which a synthetic wedge has been masked; the network learns to fill in missing Fourier directions from features observed elsewhere in the same tomogram.
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net (Cicek-style) with custom missing-wedge masking loss.
tools.training_data: The user's own tomograms with synthetic wedge masking (no external labels). Authors validate on HIV, paraflagellar rod, neuronal-synapse tomograms.
outputs: isotropic, denoised tomogram with reduced missing-wedge artifact
tools.when_to_use: Cryo-ET visualization and segmentation when missing-wedge artifacts dominate; particularly useful before MemBrain-seg or DeePiCt.
tools.limitations: Iterative training is slow; hallucination risk (features may be reinforced); not used for sub-tomogram averaging (the wedge cannot be 'restored' for STA in a statistically meaningful way).
tools.compute: GPU with 16-24 GB VRAM; iterative training can take hours per tomogram.
tools.verification_notes: Liu Y-T, Zhang H, Wang H, Tao C-L, Bi G-Q, Zhou ZH. Nat Commun 13:6482 (2022) verified DOI 10.1038/s41467-022-33957-8. | DUP: canonical entry in stage 'data_analysis'.

tools.name: JANNI
tools.approach: Noise2Noise CNN denoiser trained at MPI Dortmund on a pool of public cryo-EM movie pairs; ships a general pretrained model and is used as a visualization aid inside crYOLO and SPHIRE.
tools.architecture: U-Net (Keras/TensorFlow).
tools.training_data: Curated MPI-Dortmund/SPHIRE corpus of cryo-EM movie even/odd pairs across multiple EMPIAR samples.
outputs: denoised micrograph used as picking aid
tools.when_to_use: Cryo-EM micrograph denoising for visualization and as input to crYOLO when raw SNR is low.
tools.limitations: JANNI itself does not have a dedicated peer-reviewed paper; described in the SPHIRE-crYOLO Communications Biology paper. Pretrained model biased toward holey carbon SPA grids.
tools.last_meaningful_update: Maintained inside MPI-Dortmund SPHIRE stack through 2023-2024.
tools.verification_notes: Wagner T et al. (2020) Commun Biol 3:61 verified PMID 32047220 / DOI 10.1038/s42003-020-0790-y. JANNI is a companion tool released alongside SPHIRE-crYOLO 1.5; no JANNI-only paper exists.

tools.name: M
tools.approach: Reference-based multi-particle refinement framework that jointly models per-frame and per-tilt sample deformation (spatiotemporal B-spline grids) and corrects electron-optical aberrations; bridges frame-series SPA and tilt-series cryo-ET in one optimizer. Strictly speaking spans processing and STA.
inputs: RELION-style particle STAR with refined poses
outputs: jointly refined trajectories, CTF, and aberration parameters
tools.when_to_use: When pushing tilt-series STA toward sub-4 A or aligning per-frame motion across a multi-particle population (e.g., bacterial 70S in cells at 3.5 A).
tools.limitations: High GPU memory requirement; pipeline tightly coupled to Warp/RELION.
tools.compute: CUDA GPU, ideally 24-48 GB VRAM for full tilt-series jobs.
tools.last_meaningful_update: Warp 2.x WarpTools refresh (2024); see also M-Tools.
tools.verification_notes: Tegunov D, Xue L, Dienemann C, Cramer P, Mahamid J. Nat Methods 18:186-193 (2021) verified PMID 33542511.

tools.name: MicAssess
tools.approach: CNN-based binary (and hierarchical sub-) classification of motion-corrected micrographs into 'good' and 'bad' categories using a ResNet-34 feature extractor and a fully-connected classifier. Designed for unattended on-the-fly micrograph curation.
tools.architecture: ResNet-34 backbone + fully-connected classifier with dropout.
tools.training_data: Labeled micrographs from the Cianfrocco lab and partner facilities; ~10K-scale binary good/bad labels.

citation.venue: IUCrJ (high-throughput cryo-EM enabled by user-free preprocessing routines)

outputs: good/bad label, hierarchical sub-class label, confidence
tools.when_to_use: Automated micrograph curation at the start of an SPA pipeline; especially useful at high-throughput facilities running unattended sessions.
tools.limitations: Trained on holey-carbon SPA data; performance degrades on novel grid types; classifier-level metrics do not directly predict downstream FSC.
tools.compute: Single GPU recommended; CPU inference feasible.
tools.last_meaningful_update: MicAssess 1.0 (2021); see Miffi 2024 for the successor effort.
tools.verification_notes: Li Y et al. IUCrJ 7:1119-1129 (2020) verified PMID 32294468. Original paper title: 'High-throughput cryo-EM enabled by user-free preprocessing routines.'

tools.name: Miffi
tools.approach: CNN micrograph filter that consumes both the real-space image and its 2D power spectrum as a two-channel input; uses transfer learning from ImageNet weights and fine-tunes on cryo-EM labels. Improves over MicAssess on crystalline ice and drift cases by exposing the Fourier signature.
tools.architecture: ConvNeXt (CNN) backbone with two-channel (real + power-spectrum) input and a multi-label classification head.
tools.training_data: Curated micrograph labels with several rejection categories (crystalline ice, drift, contamination, etc.); fine-tuned from ImageNet-pretrained ConvNeXt.
tools.when_to_use: Improved replacement for MicAssess where Fourier-domain artifacts (ice rings, drift) are common.
tools.limitations: Multi-label model still trained on holey-carbon SPA data; user-side fine-tuning recommended for unusual grid types.
tools.compute: Single GPU (~3 micrographs/s on a modern card); CPU possible at ~3 s/micrograph.
tools.verification_notes: Liao H, Ando-lab. JSB 216(2):108072 (2024) verified PMID 38405773 / DOI 10.1016/j.jsb.2024.108072. The Ando lab repo and Scipion plugin both reference this paper.

tools.name: MotionCor2
tools.approach: Patch-based local motion correction of beam-induced sample movement; whole-frame translation followed by anisotropic local motion modeled per patch, with optional exposure-dependent dose weighting (Grant & Grigorieff filter).
tools.when_to_use: Default GPU motion correction for SPA and tilt-series movie frames; integrated by virtually all SPA pipelines (RELION, cryoSPARC, Scipion, Warp).
tools.limitations: Classical patch optimization; cannot recover information lost to extreme beam-induced motion; requires CUDA-capable GPU; original release closed source binary (UCSF), MotionCor3 (CZII) is now open source.
tools.compute: Single CUDA GPU (Maxwell+); 4-8 GB VRAM usually sufficient per movie.
tools.license: Free academic (UCSF binary); MotionCor3 is BSD-3 via CZII.
tools.last_meaningful_update: 2020 (UCSF v1.5.0); see MotionCor3 for active line.
tools.verification_notes: Zheng SQ et al. Nat Methods 14:331-332 (2017) verified PMID 28250466 / DOI 10.1038/nmeth.4193.

tools.name: MotionCor3
tools.approach: Re-implementation and extension of MotionCor2 by the original UCSF authors at CZII: multi-GPU acceleration, native EER support, integrated CTF estimation, and support for cryo-ET tilt-series movies.

citation.venue: Nature Methods (canonical MotionCor2 paper; MotionCor3 is the same lineage)

tools.when_to_use: Drop-in replacement for MotionCor2 on modern direct-detector data, especially Falcon 4i EER movies and tilt-series movies; preferred for open-source workflows.
tools.limitations: No dedicated peer-reviewed paper distinct from MotionCor2; cite MotionCor2 for methodology and reference the repository for the v3 release.
tools.last_meaningful_update: Active commits at github.com/czimaginginstitute/MotionCor3 as of 2025-2026.
tools.verification_notes: No standalone MotionCor3 paper exists; repository README cites the 2017 MotionCor2 Nat Methods paper. CZ Imaging Institute hosts the maintained fork.

tools.name: Noise2Noise
tools.approach: Foundational training paradigm: learn to denoise by mapping one noisy realization of a signal to another noisy realization; with zero-mean independent noise the L2-trained network converges toward the clean signal in expectation. Underlies cryo-CARE and Topaz-Denoise.
tools.architecture: Generic CNN/U-Net (architecture-agnostic; the contribution is the loss/training scheme).
tools.training_data: Paired noisy realizations of the same image; in cryo-EM these are even/odd movie-frame sums or even/odd tomograms.
tools.when_to_use: Reference for the training paradigm; not used directly in cryo-EM but cited as the methodological foundation of cryoCARE, Topaz-Denoise, JANNI, and DenoisET.
tools.limitations: Requires that the noise across realizations is independent and zero-mean; violated when even/odd halves are correlated through shared imaging artifacts.
tools.compute: Single GPU; reference implementation in TensorFlow.
tools.last_meaningful_update: Original 2018 ICML paper; no active development of NVlabs/noise2noise.
tools.verification_notes: Lehtinen J et al. ICML 2018 (PMLR 80) verified arXiv 1803.04189; the proceedings entry is the canonical citation.

tools.name: Noise2Self
tools.approach: Self-supervised denoising via 'J-invariance': partitions pixels into groups and trains the network to predict each group from the others, so the predicted output is independent of the held-out group. Generalizes N2V and applies to any denoising function (not just CNNs).
tools.architecture: Architecture-agnostic (CNN, ViT, median filter all permitted); reference uses U-Net.
tools.training_data: The user's own noisy stack.
tools.when_to_use: Methodological reference; occasionally used in vEM denoising pipelines and single-cell imaging.
tools.limitations: Requires correct partition into J-invariant groups; assumes noise independence across groups.
tools.last_meaningful_update: 2019 paper; CZ Biohub repo lightly maintained.
tools.verification_notes: Batson J & Royer L. ICML 2019 (PMLR 97) verified arXiv 1901.11365.

tools.name: Noise2Void
tools.approach: Blind-spot self-supervised denoising: at each training step a random pixel is masked and the network is trained to predict it from its neighborhood. Eliminates the need for paired data; assumes pixel-independent noise.
tools.architecture: Generic 2D/3D U-Net (CSBDeep/JUG-lab implementation).
tools.training_data: The user's own noisy stack; no labels and no pairs.
tools.when_to_use: When paired noisy realizations are unavailable, e.g. legacy datasets without even/odd splits or single-tilt vEM stacks.
tools.limitations: Assumes spatially uncorrelated noise (often violated in EM after motion correction or detector binning); typically weaker than Noise2Noise when pairs are available.
tools.verification_notes: Krull A, Buchholz T-O, Jug F. CVPR 2019:2129-2137 verified.

tools.name: novaCTF
tools.approach: 3D-CTF correction for cryo-ET tomograms by computing per-tilt, depth-dependent CTF-corrected projections before back-projection. Increases sub-tomogram averaging resolution by accounting for the varying defocus across thick samples.
inputs: tilt-series stack with per-tilt CTF estimates
tools.when_to_use: Pre-STA tomogram reconstruction when 3D-CTF correction is required for sub-4 A subtomogram averages; standard step in many high-resolution in-situ cryo-ET pipelines.
tools.limitations: Computationally heavier than 2D-CTF correction; assumes per-tilt CTF parameters are accurately estimated upstream.
tools.last_meaningful_update: Stable; tied to Turonova lab releases.
tools.verification_notes: Turonova B, Schur FKM, Wan W, Briggs JAG. JSB 199:187-195 (2017) verified PMID 28743638. | DUP: canonical entry in stage 'data_analysis'.

tools.name: Patch CTF (cryoSPARC)
tools.approach: Patch-wise CTF estimation across the micrograph that produces a spatially varying defocus map; corresponds operationally to local CTF in Warp/Gctf. Documented in the cryoSPARC guide.
outputs: defocus map, tilt, astigmatism per patch
tools.when_to_use: When cryoSPARC is the primary processing suite; avoids tool-juggling.
tools.limitations: Closed source; subset of details documented in published form.
tools.verification_notes: Foundational paper Punjani et al. 2017. Patch CTF feature documented in the cryoSPARC guide; not a separately published algorithm.

tools.name: RELION 5 tomography
tools.approach: Cryo-ET pipeline within RELION-5 that wraps CTFFIND4 for CTF, IMOD/AreTomo for alignment, and cryoCARE for tomogram denoising; carries the data forward through particle picking, subtomogram averaging, multi-body refinement and Blush-regularised reconstruction to atomic model building (with ModelAngelo).
tools.architecture: Wrappers around external tools + Blush regularization (denoising CNN) at the refinement step.
tools.training_paradigm: supervised (Blush CNN); none_classical for the wrappers
tools.training_data: Blush trained on EMDB half-map pairs; other modules are non-learned wrappers.
tools.when_to_use: End-to-end cryo-ET in a single open-source package; preferred when wanting tight integration of Blush regularisation and ModelAngelo model building for STA at sub-4 Å.
tools.limitations: Heavier installation than standalone tools; performance can lag GPU-only pipelines like Warp 2; CTF wrapper still routes through CTFFIND4.
tools.last_meaningful_update: Burt et al. 2024 FEBS Open Bio; RELION 5.0 stable 2024-2025.
tools.verification_notes: Burt A, Toader B, Warshamanage R, von Kügelgen A, Pyle E, Zivanov J, Kimanius D, Bharat TAM, Scheres SHW. FEBS Open Bio 14(11):1788-1804 (2024). PMID 39147729, DOI 10.1002/2211-5463.13873.

tools.name: RELION MotionCor (own implementation)
tools.approach: RELION's in-suite re-implementation of the MotionCor2 algorithm (patch-based whole-frame plus local trajectory fitting). Used when running MotionCor2 binaries is undesirable; behaves equivalently for practical purposes.

citation.venue: IUCrJ (Bayesian polishing paper, which describes RELION's motion-correction stack)

tools.when_to_use: Inside RELION when an external MotionCor binary is unavailable; gives users a fully integrated, scriptable run.
tools.limitations: Slower per micrograph than MotionCor2/3 in some benchmarks; identical algorithmic ceiling.
tools.verification_notes: Implementation distinct from MotionCor2 binary but algorithm follows Zheng 2017; canonical implementation citation is Zivanov 2019 IUCrJ alongside the original Scheres 2012 RELION paper.

tools.name: REST
tools.approach: Supervised translation from low-quality to high-quality density: a 3D CNN learns a mapping where the high-quality target is a sub-tomogram-averaged class average and the low-quality input is the raw extracted sub-tomogram; transfer to the whole tomogram for denoising and missing-wedge compensation.
tools.architecture: Custom 3D encoder-decoder with residual blocks.
tools.training_data: Sub-tomogram pairs of (raw, averaged class) for one or several target macromolecules; e.g. nucleosomes in cryo-FIB nuclei sections.
inputs: paired raw + averaged sub-tomograms for training
tools.when_to_use: When the user has a well-averaged structure for the target macromolecule and wants to inspect per-particle states without explicit STA.
tools.limitations: Requires a target structure to define 'clean'; risk of biasing tomograms toward the training class.
tools.verification_notes: Zhang H, Li Y, Liu Y et al. Nat Commun 14:2937 (2023) verified PMID 37217501.

tools.name: Smart EPU AI features (Thermo Fisher)
tools.approach: Vendor-internal AI hole picking, ice-thickness classification, and on-the-fly CTF-based rejection inside the Thermo Fisher EPU acquisition software; spans acquisition and early processing. Architecture and training details are proprietary; performance documented in white papers and conference talks.
tools.architecture: Proprietary CNN classifiers and detectors (likely ResNet/ViT variants); not publicly disclosed.
tools.training_data: Thermo Fisher internal labeled corpus; not released.

citation.venue: Thermo Fisher Scientific product documentation / white papers

outputs: scored holes/squares, live CTF-based rejection labels
tools.when_to_use: Thermo Fisher Krios/Glacios facilities using EPU as the acquisition front-end and wanting automated quality filtering.
tools.limitations: Vendor-only; no peer-reviewed validation; not portable across instrument vendors; opaque to external audit.
tools.verification_notes: No peer-reviewed publication; flag as vendor-only in the chapter. White-paper citations exist but are not primary sources.

tools.name: SOFIMA
tools.approach: Scalable optical-flow-based image montage and alignment for very large EM volumes: dense optical flow estimates correspondences between images, then an elastic-mesh solver regularizes the flow to produce smooth, physically plausible alignment. JAX implementation with GPU acceleration.
tools.architecture: Classical optical flow + elastic mesh solver, but implemented in JAX so GPU-accelerated; not strictly a deep network.

citation.venue: Zenodo (software release; no dedicated journal paper as of 2026-05-18)

tools.when_to_use: Connectomics-scale serial-section EM alignment and FIB-SEM volume registration where TrakEM2/AlignTK do not scale; canonical at Janelia and Google connectomics groups.
tools.limitations: No peer-reviewed methods paper at the time of writing; cite the Zenodo release and the project-paper methods sections that use SOFIMA (e.g., Petascale pipeline 2024). Field is shifting toward SOFIMA as the de facto large-volume aligner.
tools.compute: GPU acceleration via JAX; multi-node for petascale jobs.
tools.last_meaningful_update: Active commits in 2024-2025; Zenodo v0.1 released January 2024.
tools.verification_notes: SOFIMA is published as software, not yet as a dedicated method paper. Cite the Zenodo DOI (10.5281/zenodo.10534541) and the Macrina et al. 2024 'Petascale pipeline' or related project papers that document its use. Flag for follow-up: confirm whether a method paper appears 2026-2027.

tools.name: spIsoNet
tools.approach: Self-supervised 3D CNN that uses well-sampled views to recover information in under-sampled Fourier directions, mitigating the preferred-orientation problem in SPA and the missing-wedge in subtomogram averaging. Adds a misalignment-correction module that refines particle poses during iterative refinement.
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net (IsoNet lineage) with anisotropy-correction and misalignment-correction heads.
tools.training_data: Per-dataset; no pretrained model required.
tools.when_to_use: Datasets with strong preferred orientation (membrane proteins on air-water interface) or missing-wedge dominated STA; recommended as a late-stage corrective post-refinement.
tools.limitations: Improvements depend on residual signal in under-sampled directions; aggressive use can hallucinate features (use half-map FSC to validate).
tools.compute: 1 GPU (>=16 GB VRAM); fast compared to cryoDRGN-class methods.
tools.verification_notes: Liu YT, Zhang H, Wang H, Tao CL, Bi GQ, Zhou ZH. Nat Methods 21(11):2078-2087 (2024). PMID 38645074. Also covers cryo-ET preferred-orientation correction.

tools.name: Summovie
tools.approach: Applies the resolution- and dose-dependent exposure filter from Grant & Grigorieff 2015 to a frame stack already aligned (typically by Unblur) and emits a dose-weighted micrograph sum.
tools.when_to_use: Drop-in dose weighting step when motion correction was performed by another tool that did not apply the filter; commonly used inside cisTEM.
tools.limitations: Companion to Unblur; not a motion corrector itself; relies on the original cumulative-dose model.
tools.last_meaningful_update: Maintenance only; superseded operationally by MotionCor2's built-in dose weighting.
tools.verification_notes: Same canonical paper as Unblur (Grant & Grigorieff 2015).

tools.name: TomoSegMemTV
tools.approach: Tensor-voting-based membrane enhancement: anisotropic propagation of local structural orientation information through the tomogram, strengthening membrane-like voxels and bridging gaps; foundational classical pre-processing for membrane segmentation. Not strictly a denoiser but functions as a structure-preserving filter.
tools.when_to_use: Classical baseline before MemBrain-seg; useful on tomograms with structured but noisy membranes; pairs with PySeg.
tools.limitations: Parameter-sensitive; MATLAB-based reference implementation; outperformed by ML segmenters on most modern data.
tools.last_meaningful_update: Last meaningful release ~2018; primary updates now happen in PySeg.
tools.verification_notes: Martinez-Sanchez A, Garcia I, Asano S, Lucic V, Fernandez J-J. JSB 186:49-61 (2014) verified PMID 24625523.

tools.name: Topaz-Denoise
tools.approach: General-purpose deep denoiser for cryo-EM micrographs (2D) and cryo-ET tomograms (3D); supervised on real even/odd splits and synthetic noise pairs across many EMPIAR datasets; ships pretrained 2D and 3D models that can be applied zero-shot.
tools.architecture: 2D U-Net (Affine-NN encoder) and 3D U-Net variants.
tools.training_data: Thousands of micrographs across EMPIAR plus in-house data; for 3D, paired even/odd reconstructions from a curated set of tomograms.
tools.when_to_use: Drop-in pretrained denoising for visualization, particle picking aids, and downstream segmentation; particularly useful when paired even/odd realizations are not available.
tools.limitations: Models can over-smooth high-frequency biological signal; not validated by downstream FSC for SPA refinement; pretrained corpus may underrepresent membrane proteins or unusual grid types.
tools.compute: Single GPU; <=8 GB VRAM for 2D, 16+ GB for 3D.
tools.verification_notes: Bepler T, Kelley K, Noble AJ, Berger B. Nat Commun 11:5208 (2020) verified PMID 33060581 / DOI 10.1038/s41467-020-18952-1. | CORRECTION: Expert flagged the 3D Topaz-Denoise variant as missing. Verification: the 3D mode is in the same Bepler et al. 2020 Nat Commun paper as the 2D mode, not a separate publication. Update existing entry instead of creating a new one.

approach + verification_notes (add 3D mo.approach_addendum: Includes a 3D tomogram-denoising mode (Topaz-Denoise-3D) trained for cryo-ET volumes. The 2D and 3D modes share the same Noise2Noise self-supervised paradigm; the 3D variant operates on even/odd-frame half-tomograms.
approach + verification_notes (add 3D mo.verification_notes_addendum: Bepler T, Kelley K, Noble AJ, Berger B. 'Topaz-Denoise: general deep denoising models for cryo-EM and cryo-ET.' Nat Commun 11:5208 (2020). DOI 10.1038/s41467-020-18952-1. Same Nat Commun paper covers both 2D micrograph and 3D tomogram denoising; the expert gap suggesting a separate Nat Methods publication is incorrect — it is Nat Commun 2020.

tools.name: TrakEM2
tools.approach: Fiji-based serial-section EM montage and alignment: SIFT-based linear alignment followed by elastic alignment with mesh-based non-linear warping to compensate for section deformations. Supports manual proofreading.
tools.when_to_use: Classical reference for ssTEM/array-tomography montage and alignment; pre-connectomics workhorse and still used for small-to-medium volumes.
tools.limitations: Scales poorly beyond ~teravoxel volumes; superseded by SOFIMA / petascale pipelines for connectomics-scale data.
tools.verification_notes: Cardona A, Saalfeld S, Schindelin J, Arganda-Carreras I, Preibisch S, Longair M, Tomancak P, Hartenstein V, Douglas RJ. PLoS ONE 7:e38011 (2012) verified PMID 22723842.

tools.name: Unblur
tools.approach: Iterative whole-frame translational alignment of movie frames against running sum; pairs with Summovie for exposure-dependent filtering. Foundational reference for the dose-weighting filter design.
tools.when_to_use: CPU-only motion correction within cisTEM and Frealign workflows; canonical reference for exposure-weighted summation.
tools.limitations: Whole-frame only (no per-particle local trajectories); slower than GPU MotionCor on large modern movies.
tools.last_meaningful_update: Folded into cisTEM ~2018; standalone binaries still distributed.
tools.verification_notes: Grant & Grigorieff (2015) eLife 4:e06980 verified PMID 26023829 / DOI 10.7554/eLife.06980. The paper introduces both the rotavirus VP6 result and the dose-weighting exposure filter used widely thereafter.

tools.name: Warp
tools.approach: Real-time preprocessing suite: motion correction with spatiotemporal B-spline deformation grids, joint local CTF estimation, deep-learning micrograph denoising (BoxNet/3D CNN), and deep-learning particle picking (BoxNet). For tilt series, jointly refines per-tilt motion and CTF.
tools.architecture: U-Net-style CNNs for picking/denoising (BoxNet); classical optimization for motion and CTF grids.
tools.training_data: Curated EMPIAR micrographs annotated by the authors for picking; denoiser uses paired even/odd frames (Noise2Noise self-supervision).
tools.when_to_use: Live and offline preprocessing for both SPA and cryo-ET; widely used when joint optimization of motion and CTF is desired or when M is downstream.
tools.limitations: Windows-centric historically (Linux build improved post-2022); BoxNet pretrained models biased toward soluble proteins on holey carbon.
tools.compute: Single CUDA GPU (>=8 GB); benefits from 24-48 GB on EER movies.
tools.license: GPLv3 (Warp); some downstream M components separately licensed.
tools.last_meaningful_update: WarpTools / Warp 2.x rewrite (2024) brought multi-platform builds and tighter M integration.
tools.verification_notes: Tegunov D & Cramer P (2019) Nat Methods 16:1146-1152 verified PMID 31591575. The 2024 WarpTools rewrite is documented in Tegunov et al. preprints; cite the 2019 paper for canonical methodology.

tools.name: Warp 2 / WarpTools
tools.approach: Major Linux-native rewrite of Warp (2023-2024) providing CLI tools (WarpTools, MTools, MCore) for movie alignment, CTF, particle picking (BoxNet), tomogram reconstruction, and per-particle refinement; includes Noise2Map denoising and tighter integration with M and RELION-5/cryoSPARC.
tools.architecture: BoxNet U-Net 2D/3D for picking; classical motion/CTF backbones; Noise2Map (Noise2Noise-style) for denoising.
tools.training_data: BoxNet: curated EMPIAR-derived particle annotations; Noise2Map: per-dataset even/odd splits.
tools.when_to_use: Default Linux preprocessing for cryo-ET and SPA pipelines integrating with M, RELION-5 and cryoSPARC; preferred when wanting a unified CLI/GPU stack on cluster.
tools.limitations: No standalone Warp-2 methods paper yet; users reliant on Tegunov 2019 (Warp 1) and Tegunov 2021 (M) for citation; BoxNet generalisation outside training distribution remains an issue.
tools.last_meaningful_update: Warp 2.0 released 2024; ongoing maintenance at Genentech / Cramer lab.
tools.verification_notes: Original Warp paper: Tegunov D, Cramer P. Nat Methods 16:1146-1152 (2019), PMID 31591575. M paper: Tegunov D et al. Nat Methods 18:186-193 (2021), PMID 33542514. No dedicated Warp 2.0 publication located as of 2026-05; the entry treats Warp 2 as an active fork of the same software family. Update the existing Warp processing entry accordingly.

tools.name: 3D U-Net (Cicek)
tools.approach: Volumetric segmentation U-Net learned from sparse annotations (annotate a few slices, network densely segments the volume); ancestor of nearly all 3D vEM networks.
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net (symmetric encoder-decoder with skip connections)
tools.training_data: Xenopus kidney confocal (original demonstration); used widely in EM by community since
tools.when_to_use: Reference 3D architecture; underlies almost every vEM and cryo-ET segmentation tool.
tools.limitations: Pure 3D U-Net is now superseded by nnU-Net's auto-config; cited for the architecture, not for direct use.
tools.verification_notes: MICCAI 2016; arXiv 1606.06650.

tools.name: Ais
tools.approach: Unified GUI tool for cryo-ET segmentation: in-app annotation, CNN training, 3D visualisation, mesh/particle export.
tools.architecture: Various CNNs (U-Net, ResUNet) trained in-app
tools.training_data: User-supplied; ships pretrained models
tools.when_to_use: When you want an integrated GUI-driven cryo-ET segmentation workflow with model training built in (rather than scripting).
tools.limitations: GUI-first; less scriptable than membrain-seg/DeePiCt.
tools.verification_notes: eLife 2024; corrected author from query (Last, Abendstein, Voortman, Sharp; NOT van der Stam).

tools.name: Amira
tools.approach: Commercial GUI-driven platform for 3D/4D biological image analysis. Combines classical segmentation primitives (thresholding, watershed, region growing, manual painting), shallow ML (random forest / pixel classifier modules), and a deep-learning workroom for 2D/3D AI segmentation. Marketed for life sciences as Amira; the same code base ships as Avizo for materials science. Heavily used in volume EM (FIB-SEM, SBEM, ssTEM, array tomography) workflows that require interactive annotation plus quantitative analysis (volumetry, mesh extraction, connectivity, statistics).
