tools.approach: Side-chain-directed validation: computes the density value at each side-chain rotamer probe position; well-fitted models have density peaks at sampled chi-1 angles, providing a model-map consistency score.
tools.when_to_use: Required validation metric for any cryo-EM publication; useful for tracking refinement progress.
tools.limitations: Side-chain-focused; less informative at <3 A or with poor side-chain density; pre-Phenix-modern.
tools.last_meaningful_update: Bundled with Phenix; standalone less active.
tools.verification_notes: Barad BA et al. Nat Methods 12:943-946 (2015). PMID 26280328, DOI 10.1038/nmeth.3541 verified.

tools.name: Frealign
tools.approach: Foundational projection-matching refinement program by Grigorieff with explicit per-particle search and likelihood-based scoring; ancestor of cisTEM's refinement engine. Still cited as the reference for several refinement metrics (Frealign score, FSC sigma).
tools.when_to_use: Legacy or reproducibility studies; mostly subsumed by cisTEM today.
tools.limitations: Standalone Frealign superseded; rarely chosen for new projects.
tools.verification_notes: Grigorieff N. Methods Enzymol 579:191-226 (2016). PMID 27572730, DOI 10.1016/bs.mie.2016.04.013 verified.

tools.name: HetSIREN
tools.approach: Real-space heterogeneous reconstruction and refinement that uses SIREN (sinusoidal-activation INR) decoders to preserve high-frequency signal in volumes while jointly disentangling pose, CTF, and conformational latent space.
tools.architecture: SIREN-based coordinate-MLP decoder; CNN encoder with disentanglement heads.
tools.training_data: Per-dataset; benchmarked on SARS-CoV-2 spike and EMPIAR sets.
tools.when_to_use: Real-space heterogeneity preserving high-frequency features; useful when Fourier-domain encoders smooth out subtle motions.
tools.limitations: Newer than cryoDRGN/3DFlex; smaller user base; SIREN training can be unstable.
tools.verification_notes: Herreros D, Mata CP, Noddings C, Irene D, Krieger J, Jiménez-Moreno A, Sorzano COS, Carazo JM. Nat Commun 16:3839 (2025). DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-59135-0; bioRxiv preprint PMID 39345408 (2024).

tools.name: IMOD (etomo)
tools.approach: Comprehensive image-processing suite for electron tomography. Fiducial-marker tracking with cross-correlation seeding, beam-tilt geometry solution, projection-matching alignment, and weighted back-projection (WBP) or SIRT reconstruction of tilt series. etomo is the GUI front end.
tools.when_to_use: Workhorse fiducial-based tilt-series alignment and tomogram reconstruction; the default when high-quality fiducials are present and for cellular cryo-ET requiring careful manual intervention.
tools.limitations: Largely manual or semi-automated alignment; not optimized for fiducial-less lamellae; reconstruction quality limited by WBP/SIRT vs CTF-corrected back-projection unless paired with novaCTF or similar.
tools.compute: CPU (multi-threaded); modest GPU acceleration for some modules.
tools.verification_notes: Kremer JR, Mastronarde DN, McIntosh JR. J Struct Biol 116:71-76 (1996). PMID 8742726, DOI 10.1006/jsbi.1996.0013 verified.

tools.name: ISOLDE
tools.approach: Interactive molecular dynamics environment for model rebuilding into low-resolution maps. Uses GPU-accelerated MD with user-controllable forces (tug, peptide-bond corrections, secondary-structure restraints) to maintain physically realistic geometry during interactive editing.
tools.when_to_use: When rebuilding into low-resolution density (4+ A) where pure gradient-based refinement gets stuck; particularly useful for difficult loops and side chains.
tools.limitations: Requires real-time GPU MD; learning curve for force application; ChimeraX-bound.

tools.name: IsoNet
tools.approach: Iterative deep-learning missing-wedge correction and denoising of cryo-electron tomograms. A 3D U-Net is trained from the data itself (using sub-tomogram masked-wedge filling and Noise2Noise pairing) to predict isotropic tomograms.
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net (Cicek-style).
tools.training_data: Per-dataset self-supervised; supplementary training on simulated tomograms; pretrained example weights provided.
tools.when_to_use: For visualization, segmentation, and template matching where missing-wedge artifacts dominate interpretation; particularly cellular tomography of membrane-bound complexes.
tools.limitations: Not appropriate as input to high-resolution STA (introduces correlated features that can bias FSC); training on each new dataset is recommended; performance on real data depends on noise model match.
tools.compute: Single high-end GPU (>=24 GB VRAM); inference faster than training.
tools.verification_notes: Liu YT, Zhang H, Wang H, Tao CL, Bi GQ, Zhou ZH. Nat Commun 13:6482 (2022). DOI 10.1038/s41467-022-33957-8 verified.

tools.name: LocalDeBlur
tools.approach: Local resolution-guided Wiener restoration of cryo-EM maps; uses MonoRes-derived local resolution map to set frequency-dependent restoration, requiring no atomic model and no manual parameter setting.
tools.when_to_use: Model-independent local sharpening; particularly useful when no good atomic model is yet built and broad local resolution variation exists (e.g., membrane proteins).
tools.limitations: Inherits MonoRes parameter sensitivity; less aggressive than DeepEMhancer for high-frequency restoration.
tools.verification_notes: Ramirez-Aportela E et al. Bioinformatics 36:765-772 (2020). PMID 31504163, DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btz671 verified.

tools.name: LocScale
tools.approach: Reference-model-based local density scaling. Computes a local Wilson scaling factor against a refined atomic model's predicted density, sharpening map regions according to local resolution.
tools.when_to_use: When a high-quality model exists and the user wants physically motivated, parameter-light sharpening; widely used at the end of refinement.
tools.limitations: Requires an atomic model (self-referential bias in the model is propagated); LocScale 2 (Bharadwaj & Jakobi) extends to model-free operation.
tools.verification_notes: Jakobi AJ, Wilmanns M, Sachse C. eLife 6:e27131 (2017). PMID 29058676, DOI 10.7554/eLife.27131 verified.

tools.name: M (multi-particle refinement)
tools.approach: Joint per-particle, per-tilt geometric, motion, and CTF refinement across an entire tomographic dataset; treats every particle in every tilt projection as an independent observation and optimizes a global model. Enabling technology for high-resolution STA (e.g., HIV capsid <3 Angstrom).
outputs: reconstructed STA volumes at improved resolution
tools.when_to_use: After initial STA in RELION or Warp; when pushing toward sub-4 Angstrom resolution from cryo-ET data of abundant in-cell targets.
tools.limitations: Computationally heavy; benefits scale with particle count; tightly coupled to Warp's preprocessing.
tools.compute: Multi-GPU recommended; 24-48 GB VRAM per GPU.
tools.verification_notes: Tegunov D, Xue L, Dienemann C, Cramer P, Mahamid J. Nat Methods 18:186-193 (2021). PMID 33542511, DOI 10.1038/s41592-020-01054-7 verified.

tools.name: ManifoldEM
tools.approach: Manifold-embedding of cryo-EM particle images (diffusion maps / NLSA) to recover continuous conformational landscapes and free-energy surfaces; predates deep-learning heterogeneity tools.
tools.when_to_use: When the user wants explicit free-energy interpretation of conformational variability; useful complement to cryoDRGN for biophysical interpretation.
tools.limitations: Computationally heavy; sensitive to noise and angular sampling; manifold interpretation requires expertise.
tools.compute: Multi-CPU; large RAM (>= 64 GB) for big datasets.
tools.verification_notes: Foundational paper: Dashti A et al. PNAS 111:17492-17497 (2014). PMID 25422427, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1419276111 verified. Methods elaboration: Frank & Ourmazd, Methods 100:61-67 (2016).

tools.name: MapQ / Q-score
tools.approach: Measures atom resolvability by comparing the radial density profile around each atom in the model to an expected Gaussian profile of unit height. Per-atom and per-residue Q-scores summarize map-model fit.
tools.when_to_use: Standard map-model validation metric for cryo-EM at near-atomic resolution; complementary to EMRinger.
tools.limitations: Q-scores depend on map sharpening; can be gamed; not informative below ~4 A.
tools.verification_notes: Pintilie G, Zhang K, Su Z, Li S, Schmid MF, Chiu W. Nat Methods 17:328-334 (2020). PMID 32601424, DOI 10.1038/s41592-020-0731-1 verified.

tools.name: MoBIE
tools.approach: Fiji plugin for sharing and exploration of multi-modal cloud-hosted big image data; combines BigDataViewer with N5/Zarr backends, segmentation overlay, and remote dataset hosting. Designed for vEM and CLEM data analysis.
inputs: N5/Zarr volumes + segmentation tables + JSON dataset descriptor
tools.when_to_use: Sharing large vEM/CLEM data with collaborators or readers; integrating segmentation outputs with raw modalities.
tools.limitations: Less responsive than Neuroglancer on very large EM volumes; Fiji-bound.

tools.name: ModelAngelo
tools.approach: Automated de novo atomic model building. CNN over local map regions proposes candidate Calpha positions and amino-acid identities; a GNN over candidate positions integrates global context; sequence-aware HMM aligns predicted residue identities to deposited sequences. Identifies proteins from sequence database when sequence unknown.
tools.architecture: Hybrid: 3D CNN feature extractor + Graph Neural Network over candidate atoms + Transformer-style residue identity head + HMM sequence alignment.
tools.training_data: EMDB/PDB pairs at 1.6-4.0 A; thousands of structures.
tools.when_to_use: First-pass de novo model building from high-resolution cryo-EM maps; especially valuable for large complexes or when sequence is unknown.
tools.limitations: Performance falls at resolutions worse than ~4 A; nucleic acids handled less well than proteins (use CryoREAD); hallucination risk in low-resolution regions.
tools.compute: Single GPU (>=12 GB VRAM); minutes per map.

tools.name: MonoRes
tools.approach: Local resolution estimation using monogenic signal analysis. Automated and parameter-free; companion MonoDir reports local directional resolution to flag anisotropy.
tools.when_to_use: Modern, parameter-free local resolution; integrates with LocalDeBlur for resolution-guided sharpening.
tools.limitations: Mask choice affects results; over-confident on highly anisotropic data without companion MonoDir.
tools.verification_notes: Vilas JL et al. Structure 26:337-344 (2018). DOI 10.1016/j.str.2017.12.018 verified.

tools.name: Multi-body refinement (RELION)
tools.approach: Refines two or more user-defined rigid bodies as independent particles linked by relative orientation priors; recovers continuous inter-domain motion via PCA on per-particle rotation parameters.
tools.when_to_use: When the user can identify discrete rigid bodies and the motion is dominated by inter-body movement (e.g., spliceosome arm rotations).
tools.limitations: Requires manual body definition; assumes intra-body rigidity; cannot model intra-body flexibility.
tools.verification_notes: Nakane T, Kimanius D, Lindahl E, Scheres SHW. eLife 7:e36861 (2018). PMID 29856314, DOI 10.7554/eLife.36861 verified.

tools.name: MWR (Missing Wedge Restoration)
tools.approach: Deep-learning missing-wedge fill predecessor to IsoNet, using a 3D U-Net trained on a small set of simulated tomograms to predict isotropic volumes from anisotropic input.
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net trained with synthetic ground-truth pairs.
tools.training_data: Simulated cryo-ET volumes from atomic models; small dataset.
tools.when_to_use: Cited as an early baseline; largely superseded by IsoNet and DeepDeWedge for practical use.
tools.limitations: Trained on simulated data only; limited generalization; modest community uptake.
tools.verification_notes: Ding G, Liu Y, Zhang R, Xin HL. Commun Biol 2:483 (2019). PMID 31840079, DOI 10.1038/s42003-019-0660-7 verified (different MWR-style approach from later DeepDeWedge).

tools.name: Neuroglancer
tools.approach: WebGL-based interactive viewer for petabyte-scale connectomics and vEM data using the 'precomputed' chunked format. Supports multi-channel rendering, segmentation overlays, and shareable URL state encoding.
tools.when_to_use: Default viewer for very large connectomics volumes (MICrONS, FlyEM, H01); essential for vEM analysis at scale.
tools.limitations: No standalone editing tools; requires data preprocessing into chunked formats; no canonical paper (cited as Google software).
tools.compute: Browser-based; data served from cloud or local server.
tools.verification_notes: No dedicated paper. Cited via github.com/google/neuroglancer in MICrONS (Cell, 2025) and other connectomics method papers.

tools.name: nextPYP
tools.approach: End-to-end scalable platform for single-particle cryo-ET: on-the-fly tilt-series preprocessing, template matching, particle-level tilt-series refinement, classification, and visualization. Optimized for cluster-scale in-situ datasets.
outputs: aligned tomograms + STA volumes + classified particle sets
tools.when_to_use: Cluster-scale in-situ cryo-ET projects with hundreds of tilt series and hundreds of thousands of particles; alternative to Warp/M when a web-front-end and managed pipeline are desired.
tools.limitations: Server-deployment overhead; less flexible than RELION-Tomo / Warp for one-off workflows.
tools.last_meaningful_update: Nat Methods 2023 publication; Nat Protocols 2025 follow-up.

tools.name: Non-uniform refinement (NU-refine)
tools.approach: cryoSPARC refinement variant that estimates a smoothly varying signal-to-noise mask and applies cross-validation-based regularization to suppress overfitting in flexible regions while preserving high-frequency signal in rigid cores.
outputs: non-uniformly refined map + local resolution improvements
tools.when_to_use: When a flexible/disordered region degrades FSC of the rigid core; standard step in many cryoSPARC pipelines.
tools.limitations: Bundled in cryoSPARC only; no open-source equivalent.
tools.verification_notes: Punjani A, Zhang H, Fleet DJ. Nat Methods 17:1214-1221 (2020). PMID 33257830, DOI 10.1038/s41592-020-00990-8 verified.

tools.name: novaCTF
tools.approach: 3D-CTF-corrected tomogram reconstruction by phase-flipping individual tilts at multiple defocus strips and recombining via weighted back-projection. Improves high-frequency contrast and is widely used as a precursor to subtomogram averaging.
tools.when_to_use: When a CTF-corrected tomogram is needed for STA or visualization beyond ~20 Angstrom resolution; standard preparation step in many cryo-ET STA pipelines.
tools.limitations: Requires accurate per-tilt CTF estimates and tilt-series alignment; CPU-bound; superseded by integrated approaches in M and AreTomo3 for live processing.
tools.compute: CPU (multi-threaded); reconstruction times tractable on standard workstation.
tools.verification_notes: Turonova B, Schur FK, Wan W, Briggs JA. J Struct Biol 199:187-195 (2017). PMID 28743638, DOI 10.1016/j.jsb.2017.07.007 verified.

tools.name: OPUS-DSD
tools.approach: Disentangled VAE for cryo-EM heterogeneity: 3D convolutional encoder-decoder that disentangles compositional and conformational variation into a smooth, low-dimensional latent space.
tools.architecture: 3D convolutional VAE encoder-decoder with disentanglement regularization.
tools.training_data: Per-dataset; benchmarked on spliceosome, ribosome, ATP synthase EMPIAR entries.
tools.when_to_use: When the user wants explicit disentanglement of compositional and conformational variability; particularly useful where assembly intermediates exist.
tools.limitations: Disentanglement criterion is a regularizer, not a proof; latent interpretation requires user judgment.
tools.verification_notes: Luo Z, Ni F, Wang Q, Ma J. Nat Methods 20:1729-1738 (2023). PMID 37813988, DOI 10.1038/s41592-023-02031-6 verified.

tools.name: PEET
tools.approach: Cross-correlation-based subtomogram averaging tool bundled with IMOD; aligns and averages particle volumes in real space with rotational sampling. Historically the entry-level STA package; commonly used for moderate-resolution biological problems.
tools.when_to_use: Quick, scriptable STA inside IMOD pipelines, especially for axoneme/flagella geometry studies where it was developed.
tools.limitations: Real-space CC alignment lags Warp/M/RELION-5 in resolution; no formal 3D-CTF treatment built in.
tools.verification_notes: Canonical PEET methodology paper: Nicastro D et al. Science 313:944-948 (2006); PEET is described as the IMOD-bundled tool. PMID 16917055 verified.

tools.name: Phenix auto_sharpen / density modification
tools.approach: phenix.auto_sharpen optimizes a B-factor sharpening to maximize map detail and connectivity; phenix.resolve_cryo_em performs density modification using statistical priors on solvent and protein density.
tools.when_to_use: When a parameter-light sharpening is needed inside a Phenix refinement pipeline; resolve_cryo_em useful at intermediate resolution to extend interpretability.
tools.limitations: auto_sharpen is sensitive to mask choice; resolve_cryo_em assumes statistical solvent priors valid for typical proteins.
tools.verification_notes: Terwilliger TC, Sobolev OV, Afonine PV, Adams PD. Acta Cryst D 74:545-559 (2018). PMID 29872002, DOI 10.1107/S2059798318004655 verified.

tools.name: Phenix real_space_refine
tools.approach: Real-space gradient-based refinement of atomic models against cryo-EM or crystallographic maps. Uses simplified target function for speed; restraints include geometry, Ramachandran, secondary-structure, and rotamer.
tools.when_to_use: Default real-space refinement step after manual editing in Coot; required for PDB deposition.
tools.limitations: Requires reasonable starting model; restraint balance affects geometry vs density fit trade-off.
tools.verification_notes: Afonine PV et al. Acta Cryst D 74:531-544 (2018). PMID 29872004, DOI 10.1107/S2059798318006551 verified.

tools.name: PyTOM / PyTOM-Match-Pick
tools.approach: Python-based toolbox for cryo-electron tomogram localization and subtomogram analysis. Template matching with adaptive scoring + subtomogram alignment and classification; PyTOM-Match-Pick (2024) modernizes the template matching component with GPU acceleration and a tophat-transform constraint.
tools.when_to_use: Template-driven particle localization where the target structure is roughly known; PyTOM-Match-Pick recommended for modern GPU pipelines.
tools.limitations: Classical template matching biases hits toward the reference; class-aware but not class-agnostic.
tools.compute: GPU for PyTOM-Match-Pick; CPU for legacy PyTOM.
tools.last_meaningful_update: PyTOM-Match-Pick (Chaillet et al. JSB X 2024-2025) active.
tools.verification_notes: Original: Hrabe T et al. J Struct Biol 178:177-188 (2012). PMID 22193517, DOI 10.1016/j.jsb.2011.12.003 verified. Match-Pick update: Chaillet ML et al. J Struct Biol X 2025 (doi:10.1016/j.yjsbx.2024.100114).

tools.name: RECOVAR
tools.approach: Bayesian PCA-style heterogeneity analysis using regularized covariance estimation in Fourier space; computes principal components of conformational variation and reconstructs each state via adaptive kernel regression.
tools.architecture: Probabilistic PCA / regularized covariance; not a deep network (linear-subspace family).
tools.training_data: Per-dataset; tested on EMPIAR-10180 spliceosome among others.
outputs: principal components + reconstructed states + latent embeddings
tools.when_to_use: When the user wants a statistically interpretable linear-subspace view of heterogeneity that scales to many particles; complementary to cryoDRGN's nonlinear latent.
tools.limitations: Linear subspace cannot capture strongly nonlinear conformational manifolds; depends on quality of upstream poses.
tools.compute: GPU (>=16 GB VRAM); faster training than cryoDRGN.
tools.last_meaningful_update: PNAS publication 2025; active development at MIT/Princeton.
tools.verification_notes: Gilles MA, Singer A. PNAS 122:e2419140122 (2025), DOI 10.1073/pnas.2419140122. PMID 37961393 is bioRxiv version; PNAS version published 2025-03. | CORRECTION: PMID 37961393 was the bioRxiv 2023 version; the PNAS publication has a different PMID. Verification of the published PMID via PubMed (search Gilles MA RECOVAR PNAS) gives PMID 40072929 for the 2025 PNAS paper. Type label adjusted for accuracy.

citation.url + type label.note: Gilles MA, Singer A. 'Cryo-EM heterogeneity analysis using regularized covariance estimation and kernel regression.' PNAS 122:e2419140122 (2025). The 'classical' label flagged by the expert is no longer in the catalog (already corrected to ML); we additionally clarify the subtype as statistical-learning to reflect that RECOVAR is not a deep network.

tools.name: RELION (1 to 5)
tools.approach: Empirical-Bayesian / maximum-a-posteriori 3D refinement of SPA images and (since v4) subtomograms. RELION 5 adds a tomography pipeline (Burt et al.) for tilt-series-level refinement of pseudo-subtomograms and ships with optional deep-learning components (Blush regularization, NN-based ab initio).
tools.architecture: Classical EM-algorithm for refinement; Blush regularizer is a CNN denoising prior applied during reconstruction.
tools.training_data: Blush trained on simulated high-quality maps; refinement itself is classical.
tools.when_to_use: Default open-source SPA refinement engine and a free alternative to cryoSPARC; RELION 5 is the choice when open-source provenance and STA workflow are both required.
tools.limitations: GUI tied to job-tree; some workflows slower than cryoSPARC; Blush is opaque about regularization strength (over-smoothing risk).
tools.compute: Multi-CPU + GPU (>=12 GB VRAM); cluster-scale recommended.
tools.last_meaningful_update: RELION 5.0 release 2024; tomography pipeline paper Burt et al. FEBS Open Bio 2024.
tools.verification_notes: Kimanius D, Dong L, Sharov G, Nakane T, Scheres SHW. Biochem J 478:4169-4185 (2021), PMID 34878504. RELION-5 tomo: Burt et al. FEBS Open Bio 14:1788-1804 (2024), DOI 10.1002/2211-5463.13873. Original RELION 1 paper: Scheres, J Mol Biol 415:406-418 (2012).

tools.name: ResMap
tools.approach: Local resolution estimation in cryo-EM density maps via local sinusoidal feature analysis; produces per-voxel resolution map without free parameters.
tools.when_to_use: Standard local-resolution report on a finalized map; widely cited in cryo-EM papers.
tools.limitations: Sensitive to mask edge effects; pre-2018 implementation; less actively maintained than MonoRes.
tools.verification_notes: Kucukelbir A, Sigworth FJ, Tagare HD. Nat Methods 11:63-65 (2014). PMID 24213166, DOI 10.1038/nmeth.2727 verified.

tools.name: Scipion
tools.approach: Workflow framework that wraps RELION, cryoSPARC, EMAN2, Xmipp, Dynamo, and many other tools behind a unified GUI/protocol abstraction. Captures provenance, supports plugin-based extension, and enables interchange between packages.
tools.when_to_use: When cross-tool comparison and provenance tracking matter (consortium-scale projects, training, reproducibility audits).
tools.limitations: Plugin upkeep lags behind individual tool releases; learning the abstraction layer adds overhead.
tools.verification_notes: de la Rosa-Trevin JM et al. J Struct Biol 195:93-99 (2016). PMID 27108186, DOI 10.1016/j.jsb.2016.04.010 verified.

tools.name: Servalcat
tools.approach: Cryo-EM single-particle refinement and difference-map calculation built on REFMAC5; provides Fo-Fc maps, half-map refinement, and a maximum-likelihood target adapted for cryo-EM.
outputs: refined model + Fo-Fc and 2Fo-Fc maps + validation metrics
tools.when_to_use: When difference-map analysis (e.g., ligands, conformational changes) is needed during refinement; cleaner half-map weighting than legacy REFMAC.
tools.limitations: Requires CCP-EM environment; learning curve for difference-map interpretation.
tools.verification_notes: Yamashita K, Palmer CM, Burnley T, Murshudov GN. Acta Cryst D 77:1282-1291 (2021). DOI 10.1107/S2059798321009475 verified.

tools.name: SIDESPLITTER
tools.approach: SNR-aware real-space filter (a modified LAFTER) applied between half-map iterations to mitigate local over-fitting while preserving half-set independence. Inserted into the refinement loop rather than applied at post-processing.
outputs: filtered half-maps for next refinement iteration
tools.when_to_use: When a refinement shows clear local over-fitting (post-process FSC drops on masking); useful for flexible protein cores.
tools.limitations: Intervention inside the refinement loop changes the reproducibility footprint; should be applied with care to avoid masking artifacts.
tools.verification_notes: Ramlaul K, Palmer CM, Nakane T, Aylett CHS. J Struct Biol 211:107545 (2020). PMID 32534144, DOI 10.1016/j.jsb.2020.107545 verified.

tools.name: STOPGAP
tools.approach: Subtomogram averaging package by Williams Wan (LMB) using a maximum-likelihood-style framework with constrained alignment and classification; designed to interoperate with Warp and RELION particles.
inputs: aligned tilt series or Warp tomograms
outputs: subtomogram average + refined poses + class volumes
tools.when_to_use: Mature STA option that integrates cleanly with Warp/RELION pipelines, especially for cellular tomography with conformational classification needs.
tools.limitations: Smaller user community than RELION-Tomo and Dynamo; published descriptor (Acta Cryst D 2024) is recent.
tools.verification_notes: STOPGAP method paper: Wan W, Khavnekar S, Wagner J. Acta Cryst D 80:336-349 (2024), DOI 10.1107/S205979832400295X. Verify URL pattern.

tools.name: TEMPy / TEMPy2
tools.approach: Python library for 3D EM density fitting and validation. Implements segment-based mutual information (SMOC), MI, CCC, ENV scores; supports rigid and flexible fitting and bundled with CCP-EM.
tools.when_to_use: Map-model validation when alternatives (Q-score, EMRinger) need triangulation; useful for fitting flexible domains.
tools.limitations: Pythonic but heavier than dedicated CLI tools; CCP-EM environment recommended.
tools.verification_notes: Original TEMPy: Farabella et al. J Appl Cryst 48:1314-1323 (2015). TEMPy2: Cragnolini T et al. Acta Cryst D 77:41-47 (2021). DOI 10.1107/S2059798320014928 verified.

tools.name: TomoBEAR
tools.approach: Configurable modular pipeline for cryo-ET preprocessing and subtomogram averaging: wraps MotionCor2, IMOD, AreTomo, Dynamo, and STOPGAP; emphasizes reproducible YAML configuration and cluster execution.
inputs: raw movies + tilt metadata + YAML config
tools.when_to_use: Reproducible cryo-ET pipelines with mixed-package backends; teaching and consortium projects.
tools.limitations: Best as a glue layer; resolution ceiling set by the wrapped engines.
tools.verification_notes: Balyschew N et al. Nat Commun 14:6543 (2023). PMID 37848413, DOI 10.1038/s41467-023-42085-w verified.

tools.name: tomoDRGN
tools.approach: Extension of the cryoDRGN coordinate-based INR framework to cryo-ET subtomograms: learns a continuous low-dimensional latent representation of conformational and compositional heterogeneity directly from picked subtomograms and reconstructs the corresponding 3D ensemble.
tools.architecture: Encoder + coordinate-MLP (INR) decoder operating on subtomograms with per-particle pose/CTF.
tools.training_data: Per-dataset; benchmarked on HIV capsid VLP and in-situ ribosome subtomograms.
tools.when_to_use: Continuous and compositional heterogeneity analysis specifically for cryo-ET subtomograms; complements cryoDRGN-ET and DRGN-AI for in-cell heterogeneity.
tools.limitations: Distinct from cryoDRGN/cryoDRGN-ET despite shared lineage; requires reliable initial poses from STA; latent interpretation is non-trivial.

tools.name: VAST (Volume Annotation and Segmentation Tool)
tools.approach: Windows-based manual segmentation and annotation tool for large EM volumes by Daniel Berger (Lichtman Lab). Supports painting, skeletonization, and export of segmentation IDs and meshes.
tools.when_to_use: Manual ground-truth annotation for vEM ML training; Lichtman lab's reference annotation tool.
tools.limitations: Windows-only; not designed for very large fully manual segmentation; superseded for large-scale work by webKnossos and Neuroglancer.
tools.verification_notes: Berger DR, Seung HS, Lichtman JW. Front Neural Circuits 12:88 (2018). PMID 30386216, DOI 10.3389/fncir.2018.00088 verified.

tools.name: Warp
tools.approach: Integrated cryo-EM preprocessing and tomogram reconstruction platform. Classical motion correction, CTF estimation, and back-projection-style tomogram generation, plus deep-learning particle picking (BoxNet 2D, BoxNet 3D for tomograms) trained on annotated EMPIAR data. M is the companion multi-particle refinement engine for global tilt-series-level refinement at the particle level.
tools.architecture: BoxNet: encoder-decoder CNN (U-Net-like) for particle detection; classical patch-based alignment for motion/CTF.
tools.training_data: Curated annotations across ~tens of EMPIAR datasets for BoxNet 2D/3D; classical components require no training.
tools.when_to_use: Single-package solution for SPA and cryo-ET preprocessing through reconstruction; pair with M for STA at top-end resolutions.
tools.limitations: Heavy Windows historical bias (now Linux-supported via Warp 2.x); BoxNet models age out as detectors/specimens evolve.
tools.compute: 1-2 GPUs (>=12 GB VRAM); RAM-heavy for large tomograms.
tools.verification_notes: Tegunov D, Cramer P. Nat Methods 16:1146-1152 (2019). DOI 10.1038/s41592-019-0580-y verified; M paper is Tegunov et al. Nat Methods 18:186-193 (2021). | DUP: canonical entry in stage 'processing'.

tools.name: webKnossos
tools.approach: Web-based platform for distributed, large-scale annotation, skeletonization, and proofreading of vEM volumes. Supports multi-user collaboration and AI-assisted skeleton/segmentation editing.
tools.when_to_use: Multi-user vEM annotation projects; teaching and proofreading at scale; cloud-deployed analyses.
tools.limitations: Server deployment for private data adds operational overhead; segmentation editing not real-time-collaborative.
tools.last_meaningful_update: Active commits 2024-2025; commercial offering via scalable minds.
tools.verification_notes: Boergens KM et al. Nat Methods 14:691-694 (2017). PMID 28604722, DOI 10.1038/nmeth.4331 verified.

tools.name: BioImage Model Zoo
tools.approach: Community resource that distributes standardized, versioned deep-learning models for bioimage analysis under a common spec (RDF YAML) so that the same weights run in ilastik, deepImageJ, ZeroCostDL4Mic, ImJoy, QuPath, napari, StarDist, CSBDeep, etc.
tools.architecture: n/a (model registry + spec)
tools.training_data: n/a
outputs: versioned, reproducible model entries usable across multiple tools
tools.when_to_use: Anywhere a pretrained vEM / cryo-EM segmentation or denoising model needs to be shared or consumed across heterogeneous user-facing tools; reproducibility infrastructure for the chapter.
tools.limitations: Coverage of cryo-ET / cryo-EM models is still uneven; spec evolves rapidly.
tools.compute: Inference cost dictated by the model, not the registry.
tools.verification_notes: Ouyang W et al. bioRxiv 2022.06.07.495102 (2022). Still preprint as of 2026-05; consortium paper update expected.

tools.name: CryoET Data Portal (CZII)
tools.approach: Open repository of standardized cryo-ET tomograms and annotations, exposed via GraphQL API and Python client; serves both as a community benchmark (CZII Object Identification Kaggle challenge 2024-2025) and as the substrate for foundation-model training pipelines.
tools.architecture: n/a (data infrastructure); hosts model outputs and competition baselines
tools.when_to_use: Any 2024-2026 cryo-ET ML project that needs training data, benchmark splits, or community baselines; reference resource for chapter discussion of data infrastructure.
tools.limitations: Annotation density varies across datasets; not all entries are equally curated; user contributions are reviewed.
tools.compute: n/a (web service); local compute for downstream training.
tools.verification_notes: Ermel U, Peck A, Yu Y, et al. 'Annotating CryoET Volumes: A Machine Learning Challenge.' bioRxiv 2024.11.04.621686 (v2 2025-08). Related Peck et al. Nat Methods 2025 phantom-dataset paper (DOI 10.1038/s41592-025-02800-5) complements this. The portal itself has no single primary publication.

tools.name: ZeroCostDL4Mic / DL4MicEverywhere
tools.approach: Notebook-based platform (originally Google Colab) that lets non-coding users train, fine-tune, and deploy U-Net, StarDist, YOLOv2, CARE, Noise2Void, Deep-STORM, fnet/pix2pix/CycleGAN and SAM models on their own data. DL4MicEverywhere (Hidalgo-Cenalmor et al., 2024 Nat Methods) packages this as portable containers for off-Colab use.
tools.architecture: Wrappers around canonical DL architectures
tools.training_data: User-supplied
outputs: trained network weights compatible with BioImage Model Zoo
tools.when_to_use: Lab-scale training of segmentation/denoising networks when no GPU cluster is available; first stop for users adopting DL in vEM/CLEM.
tools.limitations: Colab quotas/timeouts on free tier (mitigated by DL4MicEverywhere containers); not optimised for very large vEM volumes.
tools.compute: Colab GPU (free) or any container-capable host (DL4MicEverywhere).
tools.last_meaningful_update: DL4MicEverywhere Nat Methods 2024 (Hidalgo-Cenalmor I et al., DOI 10.1038/s41592-024-02295-6).
tools.verification_notes: von Chamier L, Laine RF, Jukkala J et al. Nat Commun 12:2276 (2021). PMID 33859193. DL4MicEverywhere companion publication confirmed 2024.
